652	## Workflow
653	
654	1. Confirm the request is moving an already-crystallized feature or bug fix into
655	   implementation. Use the crystallized discussion, handoff, Solo scratchpad, or
656	   Solo todo as the concrete implementation handoff. If the feature contains
657	   multiple slices, use one lightweight scratchpad as the feature roadmap and
658	   one worktree as the execution boundary. Preserve raw user-provided output
659	   samples, transcripts, screenshots, failure text, and negative examples in
660	   the scratchpad or `.orbit/loop.md` before narrowing the scope. Create the
661	   active slice Done Contract and proceed as feature owner. When execution is
662	   delegated to a different Solo project or machine than the source handoff,
663	   create a local execution-project roadmap scratchpad that links the source
664	   and mirrors the feature request, slice order, current-slice acceptance
665	   criteria, deferred slices, and open decisions. Do not prepare the worktree or
666	   spawn workers for multi-slice work until the feature roadmap scratchpad URL
667	   and mirrored roadmap contents are recorded. Do not route through retired
668	   orchestration skills.
669	2. Set up the workspace with `bin/orbit-prepare-worktree`.
670	3. If implementation started from the Codex app or another non-Solo-visible
671	   discussion surface, use Codex App To Solo Orchestrator Handoff now. The
672	   Solo-managed Codex orchestrator resumes this workflow from the assigned
673	   worktree. The app handoff session stops after delivery and first-checkpoint
674	   proof or an explicit delivery blocker.
675	4. Read the handoff, `AGENTS.md`, `HARNESS.md`, `LOOP.md.example`,
676	   `HARNESS_SIGNALS.md`, `harness-signals/README.md`,
677	   `PRODUCT_DECISIONS.md`, relevant product docs under `apps/docs/content/**`,
678	   and relevant session context under `docs/superpowers/**`. Copy
679	   `LOOP.md.example` to `.orbit/loop.md` for the active slice and fill the Done
680	   Contract before implementation. For multi-slice work, the top of
681	   `.orbit/loop.md` must link the feature roadmap scratchpad before any
682	   implementation worker is spawned. If this is a later slice in the same feature
683	   worktree, rewrite `.orbit/loop.md` for the current slice and keep earlier
684	   slice outcomes in the feature scratchpad. The Done Contract must include raw
685	   acceptance examples or a precise pointer to them, plus explicit deferrals for
686	   any part of the user's request that is not in the current slice.
687	5. Confirm owned files or domains and existing dirty work before editing.
688	6. Decide the Solo worker plan from `HARNESS.md`. First list candidate slices,
689	   verification lanes, owned files, provider resources, shared temp/state paths,
690	   and dependencies in `.orbit/loop.md`, the feature scratchpad, or the worker
691	   plan. A serial plan for isolated goals, slices, or lanes is incomplete unless
692	   it names the concrete dependency, shared state, provider capacity limit, or
693	   merge-order reason. Being part of one goal or feature is not a dependency.
694	   If two tasks are isolated, dispatch them in parallel through Solo. Treat
695	   in-memory/Pest optimization and `composer quality-check` optimization as
696	   separate lanes by default. Do not split out Docker E2E or Incus E2E lanes;
697	   agents do not run or delegate `composer test:e2e*` commands. Do not overlap
698	   full `composer quality-check` with active user-run provider E2E lanes unless
699	   shared E2E support state is proven isolated. In parallel-worker mode, forbid broad
700	   dirty-file formatters/fixers inside workers; scope formatting/checks to the
701	   worker's owned files and run broad dirty-file tooling only after worker diffs
702	   are reconciled. Add a Claude documenter/librarian worker when documentation
703	   is substantial and the docs-owned surface is clear.
704	7. If a Claude documenter/librarian worker is used, spawn it first or in
705	   parallel only after the docs-owned slice is explicit. The feature owner must
706	   inspect the docs result and accept the docs contract before code relies on it.
707	8. Spawn the Solo implementation worker(s) with the worktree path, handoff,
708	   owned scope, documentation authority, TDD requirement, focused verification,
709	   and the rule that workers must not commit, merge to `main`, or clean up the
710	   worktree unless the feature owner explicitly assigns that exact step. Require
711	   each worker's first command to prove `pwd` and `git branch --show-current`.
712	   If the agent starts in `~/orbit` or another checkout, stop it and relaunch
713	   through a Solo terminal that `cd`s into the assigned worktree before starting
714	   the agent.
715	9. Monitor workers, inspect diffs, and send correction prompts until the
716	   acceptance criteria are met or a blocker is explicit. Worker handoffs must
717	   request the complete owned outcome in one continuous feature loop: align docs
718	   when needed, create the first failing test or docs diff, implement the fix,
719	   run focused verification, and report evidence or a blocker. Do not split the
720	   worker handoff into staged-stop-only prompts, and do not ask the worker to
721	   stop after "step 1" or wait for routine feature-owner approval between
722	   normal phases. The first narrow owned diff or explicit missing-context
723	   blocker is still expected after the required local files are read. Broad
724	   discovery without that diff or blocker is a process problem to correct.
725	   After one explicit first-diff correction, if the worker still produces no
726	   diff or blocker, stand down the worker, mark the matching harness signal
727	   recurring, and replace the worker instead of letting the process stall. If a
728	   replacement worker also fails on a tiny known patch shape, the feature owner
729	   may apply the first test or docs diff directly as a documented loop
730	   exception, then update the matching signal before continuing. When a
731	   correction reveals missing durable context, triage it through
732	   `.orbit/loop.md` and `HARNESS_SIGNALS.md`. If a reviewer or human points to
733	   behavior already present in the raw request, reclassify it as a blocking
734	   contract gap unless it was explicitly deferred before editing.
735	10. Align documentation inside this worktree when the handoff identifies missing
736	   or contradictory docs. Use the Claude documenter/librarian for substantial
737	   docs-owned corrections; otherwise keep docs corrections with the worker that
738	   owns the related behavior.
739	11. For every failed verification, review comment, human correction, docs
740	   conflict, setup problem, or agent mistake encountered during the slice,
741	   search `harness-signals/` for related prior records, then decide whether it
742	   is local cleanup or a durable harness signal. If the search returns stale,
743	   overlapping, or noisy records and curation belongs to this slice, update,
744	   consolidate, retire, or delete the records using `harness-signals/README.md`.
745	   If it is durable and belongs to the current slice, create or update the
746	   signal record and update the smallest guardrail target in the same worktree.
747	   If it is durable but broader than the slice, report a scoped follow-up
748	   instead of expanding ownership.
749	12. Check whether the project-owned Orbit skill under `.agents/skills/orbit/**` is
750	   affected. Update it in the same worktree when the change alters public CLI
751	   behavior, command signatures, node roles, state families, app/workspace
752	   runtime behavior, deployment/profile/update flows, or operational guidance
753	   another LLM would need to use Orbit correctly.
754	13. Ensure the implementation worker followed TDD (see Test-Driven Development
755	    below): failing Pest tests first, literal failing output captured, then
756	    implementation. A narrative claim that a test failed is not sufficient when
757	    the failure was used to prove red.
758	14. Keep the smallest working vertical slice that makes the tests pass.
759	15. For CLI command behavior, run retained topology proof from this worktree
760	    when the behavior touches topology, VM runtime, or operator-visible command
761	    execution. For human rendering, progress, prompts, or streaming output, run
762	    CLI reviewer PTY frame analysis before user inspection. Give the user a
763	    chance to inspect the VM-observed CLI behavior only after the reviewer has
764	    summarized the confidence basis or blocker, and before any
765	    live/release-candidate deployment. If implementation changes after PTY or
766	    retained-VM evidence was captured, refresh the evidence in a new artifact
767	    directory and label older artifacts as stale in the report. If this cannot
768	    be completed, report the blocker explicitly instead of widening the release
769	    path.
770	16. For VM/node/tool/package/doctor/role-baseline behavior, run the retained
771	   Incus inspection gate from this worktree. Retained
772	   topologies sync the current worktree into a runner-host source mount and
773	   execute from each VM's runtime mirror, so they are suitable for real VM
774	   inspection. Release and verify cleanup before continuing.
775	17. Run focused in-memory verification for the active slice. For multi-slice
776	    features, do not spend prepared E2E on every internal slice by default. Run
777	    retained topology proof as the feature-level topology gate when the final
778	    branch diff needs real topology evidence. When retained topology proof is
779	    required for feature acceptance and cannot be completed, stop the loop if
780	    the blocker cannot be resolved inside this slice. Do not commit, merge,
781	    clean up, or run final loop-improvement extraction while required retained
782	    topology proof is still blocked; record the blocker, owner, and unblock
783	    condition in `.orbit/loop.md` and the report.
784	18. Run the applicable reviewer persona from the `HARNESS.md` routing table once
785	    implementation evidence exists and before accepting the slice. For
786	    documentation-heavy changes, run `.agents/review-personas/docs-librarian.md`.
787	    For CLI command changes, run `.agents/review-personas/cli-command.md`.
788	    Spawn any code-reviewer or CLI-reviewer persona as Claude Opus through Solo
789	    at medium effort: discover the enabled `Claude` tool with
790	    `list_agent_tools`, then `spawn_agent` with
791	    `extra_args=["--model", "opus", "--effort", "medium"]`. If Claude Opus is
792	    not available through Solo, stop and report the blocker instead of
793	    substituting another model.
794	    Resolve or explicitly report findings before commit.
795	    If the reviewer finds a mismatch between implementation evidence and the
796	    raw user examples, treat it as a contract mismatch first; only downgrade it
797	    to a follow-up when the Done Contract already names the deferral.
798	    For small changed-files-only reviews, prompt the reviewer for a
799	    blockers-first verdict (`No blockers` or file/line blockers) before optional
800	    suggestions. Every reviewer prompt must begin with the same checkout-proof
801	    block required for post-feature analyzers: `cd <absolute worktree path>`,
802	    `pwd`, `git branch --show-current`, and `git status --short --branch`.
803	    Require a `CHECKOUT_PROOF` line before the reviewer reads files or returns a
804	    verdict. Include the exact diff command and base the reviewer should inspect,
805	    such as `git diff HEAD -- <owned files>` for an uncommitted post-review fix,
806	    instead of leaving the reviewer to choose a broad branch comparison. Give
807	    Claude and comparable reviewers minute-scale read time when the output shows
808	    active file reads, tool use, or generation; do not interrupt productive
809	    review work just because it exceeds a short Solo wait deadline. Interrupt
810	    once with a proof-and-verdict prompt only when the reviewer is in the wrong
811	    checkout, clearly waiting for input, idle after loading context, or
812	    generating without useful progress for an extended window. If it still does
813	    not return, close or replace that reviewer and record the process finding
814	    through `harness-signals/` before proceeding only on defensible direct
815	    evidence.
816	    Reviewer findings fixed before merge are normal feature-loop work. Promote
817	    them to loop improvements only when the review process itself missed a
818	    recurring class of issue, or existing reviewer guidance would not catch the
819	    same issue next time.
820	19. Do not run artifact-backed E2E verification. If the user manually runs an
821	    artifact-backed E2E command, record the provided output or existing
822	    `.orbit/quality-gates/` artifact.
823	20. Do not run provider provision gates. If the user manually runs a provider
824	    provision command, record the provided output or existing artifact and keep
825	    it separate from the retained topology feature gate.
826	21. If PHP changed, run:
827	
828	   ```bash
829	   vendor/bin/mago format --check
830	   ```
831	
832	22. Before reporting completion, run the verification gate implied by the final
833	    diff:
834	
835	   ```bash
836	   composer docs-lint       # docs-only markdown diffs
837	   composer quality-check   # PHP or broader repo diffs
838	   ```
839	
840	    `HARNESS.md` -> `Merge Boundary Gate` is the authority for the exact
841	    finalization requirement. The gate reads the branch diff and existing
842	    `.orbit/quality-gates/` artifacts: docs-only diffs need successful
843	    docs-lint or broader quality-check evidence, other diffs need successful
844	    quality-check evidence, and production PHP diffs also need retained
845	    topology proof. Do not rerun expensive gates from the finalization check.
846	
847	23. Before committing or reporting completion, inspect the timing evidence
848	    already produced by the applicable gates:
849	
850	   ```bash
851	   composer quality-gate:final-check
852	   ```
853	
854	    This final check must not rerun Pest, `composer quality-check`, Docker E2E,
855	    Incus E2E, provision gates, or live-node commands. If timing evidence is
856	    missing, report that the timing analysis was skipped and decide whether the
857	    feature needs another gate run before merge.
858	    Finalization reads the latest matching `.orbit/quality-gates/` artifacts
859	    for docs-lint and quality-check rows and blocks missing or non-zero evidence
860	    without rerunning the gates. Retained topology proof is recorded in
861	    `.orbit/loop.md` or `.orbit/evidence/`; the finalization hook validates the
862	    row status but does not run topology commands.
863	24. Before committing or reporting completion, run a Post-Feature Session
864	    Review. Treat `.orbit/loop.md` as the canonical local final packet and
865	    point it at the feature thread or handoff, Solo worker sessions, reviewer
866	    output, retained terminal or PTY evidence when applicable, verification
867	    output, human corrections, and factual orchestrator steering notes. Record
868	    candidate signals as they appear so final review classifies an existing
869	    packet instead of reconstructing the session. Include the orchestrator
870	    Codex thread id or transcript path when available. For non-trivial loops,
871	    spawn a fresh post-feature analyzer with
872	    `.agents/review-personas/post-feature-analyzer.md`; for tiny local changes,
873	    fill the `.orbit/loop.md` final-distillation section with the no-analysis
874	    rationale. Use the analyzer report to classify each guardrail decision as
875	    correct-noop, missed, redundant, wrong-target, or deferred; then classify
876	    each candidate as local cleanup, already covered by existing
877	    `harness-signals/` records, rejected, deferred, or a new durable signal.
878	    The feature owner adjudicates the recommendation using session context.
879	    Before creating a new guardrail, check whether a later slice already
880	    absorbed the lesson in code, tests, docs, skills, signal records, or clearer
881	    failure messages; if so, classify it as `already-covered` and name that
882	    coverage. Eliminate
883	    one-off handoffs, stale historical artifacts, reviewer findings fixed
884	    before merge, and ordinary feature work before considering promotion.
885	    Required verification that cannot be completed is a `blocked` feature-loop
886	    outcome first, not a candidate signal; promote it only when the blocker
887	    exposes a recurring process gap. Fill `.orbit/loop.md` `Required
888	    verification` with explicit `passed`, `blocked`, or `not applicable` rows
889	    for retained topology proof and `composer quality-check`. A passed retained
890	    topology row must name the topology id/kind, inspected roles or nodes, exact
891	    command, and captured terminal/session or artifact evidence. Do not mark the
892	    loop `complete` or `complete + loop improvement`
893	    while any diff-required verification is blocked, pending, skipped, missing,
894	    deferred, unresolved, or not run. Update, create, curate, retire, or intentionally
895	    leave `harness-signals/` records and the smallest guardrail target only for
896	    concrete durable signals that pass the promotion gate in
897	    `HARNESS_SIGNALS.md`. Report the loop outcome as `complete`, `blocked`, or
898	    `complete + loop improvement`. If no new durable signal remains, say that
899	    in `.orbit/loop.md` and the report. Re-run the narrow check that proves any
900	    changed guardrail target is reachable. After final distillation is complete,
901	    archive the completed active `.orbit/` state into the persistent project
902	    archive home before cleanup and before any later `.orbit/loop.md` rewrite.
903	    Name the archive directory as `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<feature-slug>` in the
904	    checkout's local time. Do not use compact timestamps, `T` separators, `Z`,
905	    or UTC offsets in archive directory names.
906	    Copy every active `.orbit/` entry except `.orbit/sessions/`.
907	25. Commit the verified worktree changes on the worktree branch.
908	26. Merge the branch back into `main` from the primary `~/orbit` checkout by
909	    following `HARNESS.md` merge and cleanup boundaries. Leave `~/orbit` on
910	    updated `main`. Preserve unrelated dirty files in `~/orbit`; if they
911	    overlap with the merge, stop for direction instead of discarding them.
912	27. If release was explicitly agreed or specifically discussed as part of the
913	    crystallized scope, run the release flow after merge. Capture live topology
914	    `doctor` status before publishing a release, run `orbit update:all` after
915	    the release artifacts are accepted, run `doctor` again, compare the before
916	    and after results, and either fix regressions immediately or record scoped
917	    follow-up tasks for intentional migration work.
918	28. When the user confirms live topology behavior or explicitly says the
919	    feature is complete, run feature completion cleanup: archive the feature
920	    scratchpad, close or resolve related Solo todos, and stand down related
921	    Solo agents or retained terminals. If the completed active `.orbit/` session
922	    has not already been archived, archive it per `HARNESS.md` before cleanup.
923	    Keep this scoped to the feature and report anything intentionally preserved.
924	
925	## Test-Driven Development
926	
927	Orbit is a TDD project. Every behavior change ships with Pest coverage that
928	fails before the implementation lands and passes after. No exceptions for
929	"trivial" changes — if behavior is worth changing, it is worth a test.
930	
931	Normal feature work follows a staged verification model:
932	
933	- **Pest unit/feature tests** in `tests/Unit/` or `tests/Feature/` that pin the
934	  internal contract: command output shape, JSON schema, validation, branching
935	  logic, error paths. These run under `php artisan test --compact`.
936	- **Source/dev topology checks** for behavior that needs a live topology during
937	  iteration. Use source-mounted Docker feature tests or retained Incus dev
938	  topologies for fast diagnosis, then codify the finding in Pest.
939	  - Incus: `composer e2e:incus -- --start --topology=<kind>` acquires a
940	    retained disposable topology. `composer e2e:incus -- --live
941	    --topology=<kind>` additionally mints a local operator identity and can
942	    bring up a local WireGuard tunnel.
943	  - Retained/live Incus topologies mount the initiating worktree through a
944	    synced source checkout at `/home/orbit/orbit`, then execute from a VM-local
945	    runtime mirror at `/home/orbit/orbit-run`. Remote Incus hosts rsync the
946	    current worktree to `/tmp/orbit-e2e-sources/<worktree>-<hash>` before
947	    acquisition, then mount that synced checkout. After local edits, use
948	    `composer e2e:incus -- --sync --id=<id>` to refresh the source mount and
949	    runtime mirrors. Keep the local worktree as source of truth; VM-side mirror
950	    edits are disposable unless copied back explicitly. Node-local mutable
951	    Orbit state remains under `/home/orbit/.config/orbit`.
952	  - Use retained/live Incus topologies to develop and test against real VM
953	    behavior. For VM/node/tool/package/doctor/role-baseline changes, this
954	    retained check is a required feature-completion gate, not an optional
955	    diagnostic.
956	  - CLI command changes always use the retained ingress VM Solo-terminal gate
957	    after focused Pest coverage and before live/release-candidate deployment.
958	    Prove the command behavior manually from `/home/orbit/orbit-run` inside the
959	    retained ingress VM. Use
960	    `./apps/cli/orbit` for source-mounted proof unless you first verify that
961	    `/usr/local/bin/orbit` resolves to the source checkout; use the installed
962	    binary only for release-candidate or live-node proof. Keep that Solo
963	    terminal open through feature completion, leave it available afterward, and
964	    give the user a chance to inspect it.
965	  - Release retained topologies with `composer e2e:incus -- --stop --id=<id>`
966	    or `composer e2e:incus -- --stop --all` when finished.
967	- **Source-prepared feature E2E** via `composer test:e2e` or a provider lane
968	  (`composer test:e2e:docker` / `composer test:e2e:incus`) is manual-only. The
969	  user may run these commands from a shell; agents must not run or delegate
970	  them. These lanes consume prepared topologies containing the current source
971	  and write timing artifacts when the user runs them.
972	- **Artifact-backed feature E2E** is also manual-only. When the user runs it,
973	  it consumes the built CLI binary and gateway image.
974	- **Provider provision gates** are manual-only substrate verification commands.
975	  Docker provision refreshes Docker runtime/support images, prepared role
976	  images, Docker host artifact distribution, or Docker topology-preparation
977	  behavior. Incus provision proves the fresh VM path: installer, `node:new`,
978	  base image, WireGuard, systemd, package installation, and host mutation.
979	  Agents do not run provider provision commands or the aggregate
980	  `composer test:e2e:provision`. There is no standing live-node lane; see
981	  `apps/docs/content/testing/README.md` for the full lane map.
982	
983	Workflow per change:
984	
985	1. Write the failing Pest test(s) first for the contract. Do not add, update, or
986	   run E2E tests unless the user's request is specifically about maintaining the
987	   E2E test suite itself; even then, do not execute `composer test:e2e*`.
988	2. Run them and capture the exact command and failing output that proves they
989	   fail for the expected reason. Store it in `.orbit/loop.md`, the feature
990	   scratchpad, or `.orbit/evidence/` when the red state matters to review.
991	3. Implement the smallest slice that turns them green.
992	4. Re-run the smallest staged lane that proves the changed behavior before
993	   reporting completion.
994	
995	A feature is not done until the relevant in-memory checks and retained topology
996	proof pass. Provider provision gates are not part of agent-run feature
997	verification.
998	
999	## Implementation Rules
1000	
1001	- Prefer existing Orbit and Laravel patterns.
1002	- Treat current docs as product authority.
1003	- Keep docs, tests, and code aligned.
1004	- Solo implementation workers perform substantive implementation edits; the
1005	  feature owner orchestrates, reviews, verifies, commits, merges, cleans up, and
1006	  reports.
1007	- Give each worker one clear ownership boundary. If multiple boundaries are
1008	  clear and independent, use parallel workers. If a boundary is hard to state,
1009	  use one implementation worker serially instead.
1010	- Apply documentation updates in the same implementation worktree as the related
1011	  tests and code. Do not rely on a separate documentation-only implementation
1012	  pass for feature work.
1013	- Use a feature scratchpad for multi-slice feature intent, rough slice order,
1014	  slice outcomes, and final gate notes. Keep Solo todos optional; create them
1015	  only for asynchronous assignment, queueing, or explicit tracking outside the
1016	  active orchestrator thread. Missing a feature scratchpad before multi-slice
1017	  worker dispatch is a process miss; a cross-project scratchpad that only links
1018	  the source without mirroring the roadmap substance is also a process miss.
1019	  Pause, create or fix the scratchpad, and record the correction in
1020	  `.orbit/loop.md` final distillation.
1021	- Run the repo feedback loop from `.orbit/loop.md` during the active slice,
1022	  creating it from `LOOP.md.example` when needed. `.orbit/loop.md` is
1023	  current-slice state, not feature history; rewrite it when the next slice
1024	  starts and preserve prior slice outcomes in the feature scratchpad. Every
1025	  signal does not need a repository edit, but every durable signal needs either
1026	  a curated `harness-signals/` record plus a guardrail target update in this
1027	  worktree, or a scoped follow-up in the implementation report. Do not use
1028	  `.orbit/loop.md` or `HARNESS_SIGNALS.md` as event logs. Curate stale or noisy
1029	  signal records when they are in the owned scope; otherwise report a focused
1030	  curation follow-up.
1031	- Keep the project-owned Orbit skill in sync with product and implementation
1032	  changes. `.agents/skills/orbit/SKILL.md` is the concise external-LLM entry point;
1033	  `.agents/skills/orbit/references/*.md` carries command-family detail. If a change
1034	  affects how another LLM should operate Orbit, update the matching skill
1035	  reference file in the same commit. If the skill is not affected, say so in
1036	  the report instead of leaving the check implicit.
1037	- When the change lands a direction change or reversal, append a one-line entry
1038	  to `PRODUCT_DECISIONS.md` (newest first,
1039	  `- YYYY-MM-DD — <decision with topic noun>. (solo todo #NNNN)`), linking the
1040	  Solo todo being executed. Skip routine work — flags, fixes, refactors.
1041	- When a decision removes or renames a public command, flag, or product term,
1042	  also append an entry to `banned_terms` in `apps/docs/config/librarian.php`
1043	  in the same change (terms, decision line, replacement wording, allow paths).
1044	  `composer docs-lint` then fails on every stale mention of the retired term
1045	  until the docs sweep is complete, and keeps it from coming back.
1046	- Retire tests only when current docs reject the behavior or replacement coverage exists.
1047	- Stop for direction if the docs and requested behavior conflict.
1048	- Stay inside owned scope and leave unrelated dirty files untouched.
1049	- Completed work does not stay stranded in `.worktrees/`: it is committed,
1050	  merged into `main`, and cleaned up unless the user explicitly asks for a PR or
1051	  preserved branch.
1052	- Solo feature state does not stay open after the feature is accepted complete:
1053	  archive the feature scratchpad, close or resolve related Solo todos, and stop
1054	  or archive related Solo agents. Do this only after user/live acceptance, and
1055	  do not touch unrelated Solo state.
1056	
1057	## Report Shape
1058	
1059	```markdown
1060	## Implementation Report
1061	
1062	Worktree:
1063	- `.worktrees/<branch-name>` on branch `<branch>`
1064	
1065	Raw contract:
1066	- User-provided examples/transcripts preserved at: <.orbit/loop.md,
1067	  scratchpad section, prompt excerpt, or none>
1068	- Explicit deferrals: <deferred request parts with reason/owner, or none>
1069	
1070	Solo implementation delegation:
1071	- Orchestrator: <model/tool, name/process id, Solo project id, parent/source
1072	  thread pointer, or not handed off>
1073	- Worker(s): <model/tool, name/process id, parent process id when available,
1074	  and owned scope>
1075	- Corrections requested: <summary or none>
1076	
1077	Documenter/librarian delegation:
1078	- Worker: <name/process id and owned docs scope, or not used>
1079	- Docs contract status: <accepted, needs changes, blocked, or not applicable>
1080	
1081	Changed files:
1082	- <path>: <why>
1083	
1084	Product-decisions ledger:
1085	- <appended line, or none>
1086	
1087	Orbit skill:
1088	- <updated files, or not affected>
1089	
1090	Harness signals:
1091	Repeat this block for each durable signal, or write `none`.
1092	- Record: <harness-signals/path.md, follow-up path, or none>
1093	- Source: <signal source, or none>
1094	- Missing context: <context gap, or none>
1095	- Guardrail target: <updated target, follow-up target, or none>
1096	- Verification: <how the guardrail target was checked, or not applicable>
1097	- Follow-up: <scoped follow-up, or none>
1098	
1099	Reviewer personas:
1100	- <persona path>: <findings resolved, findings deferred, not applicable, or blocked>
1101	
1102	Post-feature session review:
1103	- Loop outcome: <complete, blocked, or complete + loop improvement>
1104	- Required verification:
1105	  - Retained topology proof: <passed, blocked, or not applicable with topology
1106	    id/kind, inspected roles or nodes, exact command, terminal/session/artifact
1107	    evidence, blocker, or reason>
1108	  - `composer quality-check`: <passed, blocked, or not applicable with
1109	    command/evidence, blocker, or reason>
1110	- Finalization gate fit: <why the branch diff makes docs-lint, quality-check,
1111	  and retained topology proof passed, blocked, or not applicable>
1112	- Distillation packet: <.orbit/loop.md canonical packet, not applicable, or
1113	  blocked>
1114	- Fresh post-feature analyzer: <persona/process id/verdict, not used with
1115	  rationale, or blocked>
1116	- Evidence reviewed: <feature thread, Solo workers, reviewer output,
1117	  terminal/PTY evidence, verification output, human corrections, or not
1118	  applicable>
1119	- Session archive: <path/status, not yet needed before cleanup or loop rewrite,
1120	  or blocked>
1121	- Mistakes found after readiness claims: <summary or none>
1122	- Candidate classifications: <promote/already-covered/reject/defer summary, or
1123	  none>
1124	- Existing signals covered: <harness-signals paths or none>
1125	- Accepted durable signal or guardrail change: <record/target and verification,
1126	  or none>
1127	- Rejected or already-covered signals: <summary and rationale, or none>
1128	- Deferred follow-ups: <scoped follow-up, owner, trigger, or none>
1129	- No-new-signal rationale: <why local cleanup, existing guardrails, rejection,
1130	  or deferral was enough, or not applicable>
1131	
1132	Tests:
1133	- Pest unit/feature: <test added or changed>
1134	- Pest E2E: <not applicable, or suite-maintenance diff without execution>
1135	- Red-test evidence: <literal failing command/output path or not applicable>
1136	
1137	Verification:
1138	- `php artisan test --compact`: <result>
1139	- Retained topology proof: <topology id/kind, instance or node, terminal/session
1140	  or artifact, command results, or not applicable>
1141	- PTY frame analysis before user review: <artifact paths, launcher, exit code,
1142	  max idle gap, cadence/transcript finding, or not applicable>
1143	- User CLI verification: <confirmed, pending, blocked, or not applicable>
1144	- `composer quality-check`: <result>
1145	
1146	Merge-back:
1147	- Commit: <sha>
1148	- Main checkout: `~/orbit` on `main` at <sha>
1149	- Worktree cleanup: <status per `HARNESS.md` Feature Cleanup>
1150	
1151	Feature completion cleanup:
1152	- Completion trigger: <user live confirmation, user says complete, pending, or not applicable>
1153	- Solo scratchpad: <archived, preserved with reason, none, or pending>
1154	- Solo todos: <closed/resolved ids, preserved with reason, none, or pending>
1155	- Solo agents/terminals: <stopped/archived ids, preserved with reason, none, or pending>
1156	
1157	Blockers:
1158	- <blocker or none>
1159	
1160	Risks:
1161	- <risk or none>
1162	
1163	Next step:
1164	- <next slice or next concrete action; do not leave this implicit>

---
name: implementing-features
description: Use when the user says to implement a crystallized Orbit feature or bug fix, or when implementing an Orbit feature, bug fix, command behavior change, documentation update, project Orbit skill sync, or scoped Solo todo handoff through Solo-managed workers.
---

# Implementing Features

## Overview

Implement a scoped Orbit change from a crystallized discussion, handoff, Solo
scratchpad, or Solo todo by acting as the feature owner. The feature owner may
run in Codex CLI, the Codex app, Claude, or another capable LLM surface. Solo is
the required substrate for spawned workers and retained verification terminals.
Crystallization happens before this skill is triggered: the feature or bug fix
has already been discussed into a concrete product contract, scope, and
verification expectation. This skill starts when the user explicitly moves from
discussion to execution with wording such as `let's implement`, `start
implementation`, or an equivalent implementation request. Documentation updates
and project Orbit skill updates are implementation work here, alongside tests
and code.

## Preconditions

- The request has a clear product contract or handoff.
- Relevant docs have been checked, with gaps or contradictions captured in the
  handoff or identified during implementation.
- Acceptance criteria and verification commands are known.
- Owned files or domains are explicit enough to avoid unrelated edits.
- If the request spans multiple slices, a feature roadmap scratchpad exists and
  its `solo://` URL is known before worktree setup or worker dispatch.
- A dedicated worktree can be created for the change (see Workspace Setup
  below).
- Solo can spawn the workers or retained terminals needed for the slice. If the
  required Solo worker or verification terminal cannot be spawned, stop and
  report the blocker instead of quietly replacing that lane with untracked work.

## Orchestrator Role

The agent using this skill is the feature owner and orchestrator. It may run in
any LLM app, but delegated implementation, documentation, review, and terminal
verification lanes must be tracked through Solo when the slice calls for
subagents or retained VM proof.

Responsibilities:

- Create and own the Done Contract for the active slice when the
  user explicitly starts implementation from the current thread or app.
- Preserve the raw user contract in the handoff. If the user provided output
  samples, transcripts, screenshots, failure text, or negative examples, keep
  them in `.orbit/loop.md`, the feature scratchpad, or the worker prompt. When
  decomposing into slices, explicitly mark which parts are in scope now, which
  are deferred, and why the deferral is compatible with acceptance.
- Prepare and own the dedicated Orbit worktree.
- Read the handoff, docs, and existing code enough to define clear worker tasks.
- For multi-slice features, keep one feature scratchpad as the roadmap and one
  feature worktree as the execution boundary. Use `.orbit/loop.md` for the
  active slice only, rewriting it when the next slice starts. Before rewriting
  `.orbit/loop.md`, archive the completed active `.orbit/` state into the
  persistent project archive home defined by `HARNESS.md`, using
  `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<feature-slug>` in the checkout's local time. Do not use
  compact timestamps, `T` separators, `Z`, or UTC offsets in archive directory
  names. Copy every active `.orbit/` entry except `.orbit/sessions/`. If the
  source roadmap lives in another Solo project or machine, create a reachable
  execution-project scratchpad that links back to the source and mirrors the
  source roadmap's feature request, slice order, current-slice acceptance
  criteria, deferred slices, and open decisions before spawning workers.
- Run a dependency scan before spawning workers. If slices or verification lanes
  have disjoint ownership and neither needs the other's result, dispatch them in
  parallel through Solo by default. Use one worker serially only when ownership,
  shared state, provider capacity, or merge order cannot be stated clearly.
- Grok is the default implementation model when available, but another suitable
  Solo-managed worker may own the slice if that is the active toolchain.
- Use the Solo role matrix in `HARNESS.md` when splitting work. Spawn a Claude
  documenter/librarian worker for substantial docs-first or documentation-heavy
  slices when its ownership is separable.
- Make each worktree-scoped Solo worker prove its starting directory and branch
  before broad reads or edits: `pwd` must be the assigned worktree and
  `git branch --show-current` must match the assigned branch. If Solo
  `spawn_agent` opens at the project root, relaunch through a Solo terminal
  that first `cd`s into the worktree.
- In parallel-worker mode, do not let workers run broad dirty-file formatters
  or fixers. Workers run owned-file-only formatting/checks; the feature owner
  runs broad dirty-file tooling after worker diffs are reconciled.
- Keep docs, tests, and code for the same behavior in one worker by default.
  Split documentation and code only when the feature owner can accept the docs
  contract before code relies on it, or when ownership is genuinely independent.
- Monitor worker output, inspect diffs, ask for corrections, and keep unrelated
  dirty files untouched.
- When a Solo worker, reviewer, analyzer, or disposable terminal is no longer
  needed, serialize cleanup: capture required output or summary evidence,
  verify the artifact exists and is non-empty or record why no output is
  expected, then stop or delete the process in a separate command. Never run
  output capture and process deletion in parallel.
- Run or require the verification gates and independently read the results.
- Run applicable reviewer personas from `HARNESS.md` after implementation
  evidence exists. For documentation-heavy changes, use
  `.agents/review-personas/docs-librarian.md`; for CLI command changes, use
  `.agents/review-personas/cli-command.md` before accepting the slice.
- Build the local post-feature packet before completion, request fresh-context
  post-feature analysis when the loop was non-trivial, and adjudicate analyzer

- Follow `HARNESS.md` for final-distillation, merge-boundary, post-feature

  executable gate usage.

  feature completion cleanup, and the implementation report.

Do not make substantive implementation edits yourself unless the user explicitly
approves bypassing the Solo worker lane. Small orchestration-only edits,
conflict resolution after review, and mechanical formatting fixes are acceptable
only when they do not replace the tracked worker loop.

## Workspace Setup

Implementation happens in an isolated worktree, never directly on `main` or a
shared branch. Use `bin/orbit-prepare-worktree` from the main checkout to
create, bootstrap, and verify the worktree. Do not hand-roll these steps.

A new worktree starts empty — Orbit ignores `.env`, `vendor/`, and `.env.e2e`,
so the worktree must be bootstrapped before any test or quality-check command
will pass. Skip any of these and `php artisan test` fails at boot
(encrypted-cast tests need `APP_KEY`; E2E composer scripts source `.env.e2e`).

Orbit conventions:

- Worktrees live in `.worktrees/<branch-name>/` at the repo root. This directory
  is already gitignored.
- Name the branch and worktree directory after the feature or fix in kebab-case
  (e.g. `.worktrees/app-node-security-foundations`).
- Do all editing, test runs, and verification from inside the worktree path.

Run this from the main checkout:

```bash
bin/orbit-prepare-worktree <branch-name>
```

Use `--base=<ref>` when the todo must start from a branch other than `main`.
Do not use `--with-e2e` for feature work. CLI command changes require focused
Pest coverage plus retained topology proof when topology behavior is in scope.
The script creates or reuses `.worktrees/<branch-name>/`, installs
dependencies, prepares Laravel app state, links `.env.e2e` when available, and
runs `composer test` unless `--skip-tests` is explicitly passed.

If preparation fails, leave the worktree in place for inspection and report the
failing step instead of dispatching implementation onto a broken checkout.

## E2E Readiness And Resource Pool

This section is for reading shared E2E provider state and existing artifacts
only. Agents must not run `composer test:e2e*` commands. Normal feature
completion uses retained topology proof instead of prepared E2E.

The E2E provider pools are shared across every Orbit worktree on this machine.
Worktrees symlink `.env.e2e` back to the main checkout, so provider selection,
runner capacity, lease directories, and host pools are shared state. Read the
active providers from `.env.e2e`, not from hard-coded hostnames: Docker feature
tests use `ORBIT_E2E_DOCKER_TEST_RUNNERS`, and Incus preparation/topology work
uses the configured Incus host variables such as `ORBIT_E2E_INCUS_HOSTS` and
`ORBIT_E2E_INCUS_HOST_SLOTS`.

Active `orbit-e2e` containers, networks, volumes, VMs, or lease files on those
configured providers are normal while other features run in other worktrees.
Resource existence or container count alone is not a stale-resource signal.

When inspecting a user-run E2E lane in a worktree:

1. `composer e2e:preflight` — verifies the configured Incus host is
   reachable. This is a manual diagnostic command; do not run it as an agent
   unless the task is retained topology setup rather than E2E testing.

2. Treat the provider pool as a blocking lease pool. If the user reports a long
   wait at startup, it usually means every configured slot is currently leased
   by another worktree. Do not reap merely because resources exist on a
   provider.

3. Use host diagnostics only after a wait exceeds
   `ORBIT_E2E_SLOT_WAIT_SECONDS`, or when recovering from an interrupted run.
   Derive Docker hosts from `.env.e2e`:

   ```bash
   set -a; [ ! -f .env.e2e ] || . ./.env.e2e; set +a

   printf '%s\n' "${ORBIT_E2E_DOCKER_TEST_RUNNERS:-}" \
     | tr ',' '\n' \
     | while IFS=: read -r host slots container_cap; do
         [ -n "$host" ] || continue

         if [ "$host" = "local" ]; then
           docker ps \
             --filter "name=orbit-e2e" \
             --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}'
         else
           DOCKER_HOST="ssh://$host" docker ps \
             --filter "name=orbit-e2e" \
             --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}'
         fi
       done
   ```

   Interpret output as context only. The resources may belong to live runs from
   other worktrees.

4. If the shared pool is busy, report that the user-run command can wait or
   reduce only that command's temporary demand. For Docker, the user can pass a
   smaller `ORBIT_E2E_DOCKER_TEST_RUNNERS` value or
   `ORBIT_E2E_PARALLEL_PROCESSES=<n>` in the command environment. Do not commit
   or permanently edit `.env.e2e` just to make one worktree smaller; that file
   controls every worktree.

5. Reaping is destructive recovery, not pre-run hygiene. Use the dry run only
   as inventory, and remember that its output can include legitimate resources
   from other worktrees:

   ```bash
   composer e2e:reap-docker
   composer e2e:reap-incus
   ```

   Run with `--force` only after confirming the resources belong to an
   interrupted run you own, or after confirming no live E2E process can be using
   the configured providers:

   ```bash
   composer e2e:reap-docker -- --force
   ```

   Do not use `--older-than=0m` on shared providers unless intentionally
   deleting retained or abandoned resources you own.

The slot pool is a blocking lease pool: workers that cannot lease a slot
wait, they do not fail loudly. A long hang at the start of `composer
test:e2e:docker` or `composer test:e2e:incus` usually means the configured
pool is fully booked by another worktree, not a real failure.

## Retained Incus Inspection Gate

Retained Incus is the mandatory hands-on verification step whenever the change
touches real VM/node behavior: OS package installs, role baselines, doctor
restore, tool repair, SSH/sudo, WireGuard, systemd, host mutation, gateway API
shims, source-mounted checkout behavior, or anything that previously failed
only inside an Incus topology.

Any feature that creates or changes a CLI command must also pass a retained
ingress VM Solo-terminal gate before live/release-candidate deployment. This
includes new commands, flags, options, arguments, human output, JSON schemas,
validation, prompts, command side effects, and command-family behavior.
CLI retained topology proof must run in a Solo terminal, not only through a
detached host command or captured artifact. Keep that Solo terminal open
through feature completion and leave it available afterward. The preserved
terminal lets the user later validate the addressed CLI commands and their output.
The retained topology may be reaped after feature completion, but the Solo
terminal stays preserved as the validation anchor.

For CLI changes, use this ordering:

1. Create or update focused Pest tests for the command contract.
2. Implement the smallest slice that makes the focused command behavior work.
3. Spawn or request a Solo terminal.
4. Acquire a retained Incus topology with the relevant source-mounted VM.
5. Verify which Orbit launcher will be exercised. For source-mounted retained
   topology proof, run the command through the source checkout
   (`./apps/cli/orbit` from `/home/orbit/orbit-run`) or prove that
   `/usr/local/bin/orbit` resolves to that source checkout. For
   release-candidate or live-node proof, use the installed binary path being
   validated.
6. Open an interactive shell inside the relevant retained VM, usually the
   ingress or operator VM, before running the changed command. The Solo
   terminal should land at `/home/orbit/orbit-run` inside the VM so the user can
   watch progress, spinners, blinking indicators, prompts, and streaming output
   while the command runs.
7. Run or request CLI reviewer PTY frame analysis from the same runtime context
   before asking the user to inspect human UX/output. For retained Incus proof,
   prefer running the capture script inside the Solo terminal shell attached to
   the target VM. The reviewer inspects `summary.txt`, `chunks.jsonl`, and
   `transcript.txt` for cadence, liveness, skipped frames, wrapping, ANSI
   framing, and final shape.
8. Prove the observed human output, JSON output, prompts, failure paths, and
   side effects that changed.
9. Give the user a chance to inspect and confirm the VM-observed CLI behavior
    only after the reviewer has summarized the PTY confidence basis or exact
    remaining mismatch.
10. Then run broader quality or release-candidate flow when applicable.

Do not spend the live topology or release-candidate path on a CLI change before
this retained VM proof and user verification point. Do not treat retained Incus
as optional "extra confidence" for those changes. The retained check is the
operator-facing proof gate for feature completion.

Acquire the topology from the implementation worktree and source-mount only the
roles that need the current checkout:

```bash
composer e2e:incus -- --start --topology=<kind> --checkout-roles=<roles> --json
```

For CLI command changes, use the topology that creates a dedicated ingress VM.
Source-mount the ingress role, plus only the other roles whose current checkout
is needed for the command under test:

```bash
composer e2e:incus -- --start \
  --topology=operator_gateway_app-dev_app-prod_ingress \
  --checkout-roles=ingress \
  --json
```

Identify the target instance from the retained topology output or manifest, then
open that retained VM in a Solo terminal and stop at a VM shell prompt before
starting the command. Run the exact changed command path from
`/home/orbit/orbit-run`, covering human and `--json` output when either contract
is affected, plus the relevant failure or prompt path. Record the launcher proof
(`command -v orbit`, `readlink -f`, or the explicit `./apps/cli/orbit` source
launcher command) next to the observed output.

A host-wrapped one-shot command such as
`ssh <host> 'incus exec <instance> -- ... <orbit command>'` is useful for
machine transcripts, JSON capture, or fallback diagnosis, but it does not
satisfy the retained Solo-terminal inspection gate for human rendering. The
gate is only satisfied when the Solo terminal is attached inside the VM before
the human command starts. If the current Solo environment cannot open that
interactive VM shell, use the configured Incus host with `incus exec` as a
fallback and report that the user-inspection gate was downgraded.

Inspect through the configured Incus host from `.env.e2e`; do not assume a
host name unless the environment says so. Typical Beast-backed inspection looks
like:

```bash
ssh beast 'incus list --format csv -c ns | grep <retained-id> || true'
ssh -tt beast 'incus exec <instance> -- sudo -iu orbit bash -lc "cd /home/orbit/orbit-run && exec bash -i"'
# then run inside the VM shell:
./apps/cli/orbit <command>
ssh beast 'incus exec <instance> -- bash -lc "<host command such as gh --version>"'
```

For source-mounted Incus topologies, `/home/orbit/orbit` is the synced source
mount and `/home/orbit/orbit-run` is the VM-local runtime mirror. Run Orbit
commands from `/home/orbit/orbit-run` unless explicitly testing the source
mount itself. After local worktree edits, refresh a retained topology with:

```bash
composer e2e:incus -- --sync --id=<id>
```

That sync is one-way from the implementation worktree to the runner-host source
mount and then to each recorded VM runtime mirror. It transfers filesystem
deltas for included files to the runner host, not only Git-dirty files, and then
refreshes the VM-local runtime mirrors. Keep the implementation worktree as the
source of truth. VM-side edits in `/home/orbit/orbit-run` are scratch work and
are overwritten by the next sync; VM-side edits in `/home/orbit/orbit` mutate
the runner-host copy, not the local worktree.

`--sync` refreshes files on disk but does not reload the long-running gateway
API container. After a sync, the gateway lease container keeps serving the
pre-sync code and returns HTTP 500 on every gateway call (including paths the
change never touched, e.g. single-node `doctor`), which reads as a product
regression but is not one. Restart the gateway lease containers on the gateway
VM before re-verifying:

```bash
ssh <incus-host> 'incus exec <gateway-instance> -- bash -lc \
  "docker restart orbit-gateway-e2e-topology-lease-http orbit-gateway-e2e-topology-lease-tls"'
```

Then re-run the changed command. A 500 on an unrelated gateway path right after
`--sync` is a stale-container signal, not a code defect — restart first, then
classify.

Record the retained topology id, topology kind, checkout roles, inspected
instances, Solo terminal or fallback session, commands run, and observed result
in the Solo report. If you mutate state for a focused check, isolate unrelated
prepared-state drift first and say what was isolated.

After feature completion, release and verify retained topology cleanup:

```bash
composer e2e:incus -- --stop --id=<id> --json
ssh <incus-host> 'incus list --format csv -c ns | grep <id> || true'
```

If `--stop` misses owned instances because the retained manifest is incomplete,
delete only the owned leftovers by exact instance name, verify the grep is
empty, and report the cleanup anomaly. Do not close or archive the Solo terminal
as part of topology cleanup; preserve it for later user validation of the
command address/output transcript.

## Test-Driven Development

Orbit is a TDD project. Every behavior change ships with Pest coverage that
fails before the implementation lands and passes after. No exceptions for
"trivial" changes — if behavior is worth changing, it is worth a test.

Normal feature work follows a staged verification model:

- **Pest unit/feature tests** in `tests/Unit/` or `tests/Feature/` that pin the
  internal contract: command output shape, JSON schema, validation, branching
  logic, error paths. These run under `php artisan test --compact`.
- **Source/dev topology checks** for behavior that needs a live topology during
  iteration. Use source-mounted Docker feature tests or retained Incus dev
  topologies for fast diagnosis, then codify the finding in Pest.
  - Incus: `composer e2e:incus -- --start --topology=<kind>` acquires a
    retained disposable topology. `composer e2e:incus -- --live
    --topology=<kind>` additionally mints a local operator identity and can
    bring up a local WireGuard tunnel.
  - Retained/live Incus topologies mount the initiating worktree through a
    synced source checkout at `/home/orbit/orbit`, then execute from a VM-local
    runtime mirror at `/home/orbit/orbit-run`. Remote Incus hosts rsync the
    current worktree to `/tmp/orbit-e2e-sources/<worktree>-<hash>` before
    acquisition, then mount that synced checkout. After local edits, use
    `composer e2e:incus -- --sync --id=<id>` to refresh the source mount and
    runtime mirrors. Keep the local worktree as source of truth; VM-side mirror
    edits are disposable unless copied back explicitly. Node-local mutable
    Orbit state remains under `/home/orbit/.config/orbit`.
  - Use retained/live Incus topologies to develop and test against real VM
    behavior. For VM/node/tool/package/doctor/role-baseline changes, this
    retained check is a required feature-completion gate, not an optional
    diagnostic.
  - CLI command changes always use the retained ingress VM Solo-terminal gate
    after focused Pest coverage and before live/release-candidate deployment.
    Prove the command behavior manually from `/home/orbit/orbit-run` inside the
    retained ingress VM. Use
    `./apps/cli/orbit` for source-mounted proof unless you first verify that
    `/usr/local/bin/orbit` resolves to the source checkout; use the installed
    binary only for release-candidate or live-node proof. Keep that Solo
    terminal open through feature completion, leave it available afterward, and
    give the user a chance to inspect it.
  - Release retained topologies with `composer e2e:incus -- --stop --id=<id>`
    or `composer e2e:incus -- --stop --all` when finished.
- **Source-prepared feature E2E** via `composer test:e2e` or a provider lane
  (`composer test:e2e:docker` / `composer test:e2e:incus`) is manual-only. The
  user may run these commands from a shell; agents must not run or delegate
  them. These lanes consume prepared topologies containing the current source
  and write timing artifacts when the user runs them.
- **Artifact-backed feature E2E** is also manual-only. When the user runs it,
  it consumes the built CLI binary and gateway image.
- **Provider provision gates** are manual-only substrate verification commands.
  Docker provision refreshes Docker runtime/support images, prepared role
  images, Docker host artifact distribution, or Docker topology-preparation
  behavior. Incus provision proves the fresh VM path: installer, `node:new`,
  base image, WireGuard, systemd, package installation, and host mutation.
  Agents do not run provider provision commands or the aggregate
  `composer test:e2e:provision`. There is no standing live-node lane; see
  `apps/docs/content/testing/README.md` for the full lane map.

Workflow per change:

1. Write the failing Pest test(s) first for the contract. Do not add, update, or
   run E2E tests unless the user's request is specifically about maintaining the
   E2E test suite itself; even then, do not execute `composer test:e2e*`.
2. Run them and capture the exact command and failing output that proves they
   fail for the expected reason. Store it in `.orbit/loop.md`, the feature
   scratchpad, or `.orbit/evidence/` when the red state matters to review.
3. Implement the smallest slice that turns them green.
4. Re-run the smallest staged lane that proves the changed behavior before
   reporting completion.

A feature is not done until the relevant in-memory checks and retained topology
proof pass. Provider provision gates are not part of agent-run feature
verification.

## Implementation Rules

- Prefer existing Orbit and Laravel patterns.
- Treat current docs as product authority.
- Keep docs, tests, and code aligned.
- Solo implementation workers perform substantive implementation edits; the
  feature owner orchestrates, reviews, verifies, commits, merges, cleans up, and
  reports.
- Give each worker one clear ownership boundary. If multiple boundaries are
  clear and independent, use parallel workers. If a boundary is hard to state,
  use one implementation worker serially instead.
- Apply documentation updates in the same implementation worktree as the related
  tests and code. Do not rely on a separate documentation-only implementation
  pass for feature work.
- Use a feature scratchpad for multi-slice feature intent, rough slice order,
  slice outcomes, and final gate notes. Keep Solo todos optional; create them
  only for asynchronous assignment, queueing, or explicit tracking outside the
  active orchestrator thread. Missing a feature scratchpad before multi-slice
  worker dispatch is a process miss; a cross-project scratchpad that only links
  the source without mirroring the roadmap substance is also a process miss.
  Pause, create or fix the scratchpad, and record the correction in
  `.orbit/loop.md` final distillation.
- Run the repo feedback loop from `.orbit/loop.md` during the active slice,
  creating it from `LOOP.md.example` when needed. `.orbit/loop.md` is
  current-slice state, not feature history; rewrite it when the next slice
  starts and preserve prior slice outcomes in the feature scratchpad. Every
  signal does not need a repository edit, but every durable signal needs either
  a curated `harness-signals/` record plus a guardrail target update in this
  worktree, or a scoped follow-up in the implementation report. Do not use
  `.orbit/loop.md` or `HARNESS_SIGNALS.md` as event logs. Curate stale or noisy
  signal records when they are in the owned scope; otherwise report a focused
  curation follow-up.
- Keep the project-owned Orbit skill in sync with product and implementation
  changes. `.agents/skills/orbit/SKILL.md` is the concise external-LLM entry point;
  `.agents/skills/orbit/references/*.md` carries command-family detail. If a change
  affects how another LLM should operate Orbit, update the matching skill
  reference file in the same commit. If the skill is not affected, say so in
  the report instead of leaving the check implicit.
- When the change lands a direction change or reversal, append a one-line entry
  to `PRODUCT_DECISIONS.md` (newest first,
  `- YYYY-MM-DD — <decision with topic noun>. (solo todo #NNNN)`), linking the
  Solo todo being executed. Skip routine work — flags, fixes, refactors.
- When a decision removes or renames a public command, flag, or product term,
  also append an entry to `banned_terms` in `apps/docs/config/librarian.php`
  in the same change (terms, decision line, replacement wording, allow paths).
  `composer docs-lint` then fails on every stale mention of the retired term
  until the docs sweep is complete, and keeps it from coming back.
- Retire tests only when current docs reject the behavior or replacement coverage exists.
- Stop for direction if the docs and requested behavior conflict.
- Stay inside owned scope and leave unrelated dirty files untouched.
- Completed work does not stay stranded in `.worktrees/`: it is committed,
  merged into `main`, and cleaned up unless the user explicitly asks for a PR or
  preserved branch.
- Solo feature state does not stay open after the feature is accepted complete:
  archive the feature scratchpad, close or resolve related Solo todos, and stop
  or archive related Solo agents. Do this only after user/live acceptance, and
  do not touch unrelated Solo state.
