export const meta = {
  name: 'orbit-loop-review',
  description: 'Analyze every .orbit session (local + mini), agent transcripts from last 5 days, and loop-relevant skills for wrinkles and simplification opportunities',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Sessions', detail: 'one analyst per archived .orbit session (12 local + 26 mini)' },
    { title: 'Transcripts', detail: 'Codex/Claude/Grok implementation-cycle transcripts, chunked' },
    { title: 'Skills', detail: 'loop-relevant skills, personas, harness docs, bin helpers' },
  ],
}

const CONTEXT = [
  'Context: Orbit is an LLM-first monorepo at ~/orbit. Features are implemented through an orchestration/implementation loop:',
  'a feature orchestrator (often Codex) prepares an isolated worktree via bin/orbit-prepare-worktree, copies LOOP.md.example to .orbit/loop.md,',
  'fills a Done Contract, dispatches Solo-managed workers (Grok default implementer, Claude documenter, Claude Opus reviewer personas and a post-feature analyzer),',
  'verifies with focused Pest / composer quality-check / retained Incus topology proof for CLI-VM behavior,',
  'fills a Final Distillation section (loop outcome: complete | blocked | complete + loop improvement, plus required-verification rows),',
  'must pass bin/orbit-feature-finalization-check before merge/cleanup, merges to main,',
  'then archives active .orbit/ state into .orbit/sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<slug>/ (local time; compact timestamps, T separators, Z, or UTC offsets are FORBIDDEN by HARNESS.md),',
  'including agent-sessions/ provider transcript archives via bin/orbit-session-archive.',
  'Durable lessons are promoted into harness-signals/ records plus the smallest guardrail target (HARNESS.md, AGENTS.md, .agents/skills/*, review personas, tests).',
  'The review goal: find wrinkles and friction, ceremony that does not pay for itself, contract violations, lost self-improvement signal, and concrete simplifications that make the loop more effective.',
].join(' ')

const STYLE = 'Be concrete and evidence-based: quote short fragments (max 15 words) and name file paths. Each finding is one sentence, max 30 words. Empty arrays are fine — do not pad or invent. Your structured output is machine-consumed; no prose outside the schema.'

const SESSION_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  required: ['unit', 'machine', 'feature', 'loopOutcome', 'nameContractOk', 'packetQuality', 'frictions', 'ceremony', 'improvementIdeas'],
  properties: {
    unit: { type: 'string', description: 'session dir basename' },
    machine: { type: 'string', enum: ['local', 'mini'] },
    feature: { type: 'string', description: 'what this session implemented, max 15 words' },
    loopOutcome: { type: 'string', description: 'recorded loop outcome, or "missing"' },
    nameContractOk: { type: 'boolean', description: 'basename matches YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<slug> local-time contract' },
    agentSessionsArchived: { type: 'string', description: 'present / missing / empty-manifest — HARNESS says archives should include agent-sessions' },
    packetQuality: { type: 'string', description: 'one sentence: is Final Distillation real insight or boilerplate; are candidate signals concrete' },
    frictions: { type: 'array', maxItems: 8, items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'observed friction with evidence' },
    ceremony: { type: 'array', maxItems: 5, items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'loop bookkeeping that cost effort without visible value in this session' },
    gateIssues: { type: 'array', maxItems: 5, items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'finalization-gate / verification-row problems' },
    danglingEvidence: { type: 'array', maxItems: 5, items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'evidence pointers that no longer resolve (dead Solo ids, other-machine paths)' },
    improvementIdeas: { type: 'array', maxItems: 5, items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const TRANSCRIPT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  required: ['units', 'provider', 'machine', 'relevant', 'taskSummaries', 'frictions', 'improvementIdeas'],
  properties: {
    units: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'file/dir basenames analyzed' },
    provider: { type: 'string', enum: ['codex', 'claude', 'grok'] },
    machine: { type: 'string', enum: ['local', 'mini'] },
    relevant: { type: 'string', description: 'which units were orbit implementation/orchestration cycles vs unrelated chatter' },
    taskSummaries: { type: 'array', maxItems: 8, items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'per relevant unit: task in max 12 words' },
    frictions: { type: 'array', maxItems: 10, items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'pattern + short quoted evidence + which unit' },
    ceremonyShare: { type: 'string', description: 'rough share of the session spent on loop bookkeeping vs actual implementation, with basis' },
    userCorrections: { type: 'array', maxItems: 6, items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'places the human had to redirect/scold the agent' },
    improvementIdeas: { type: 'array', maxItems: 5, items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const SKILL_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  required: ['lane', 'findings', 'simplifications', 'updates', 'keep'],
  properties: {
    lane: { type: 'string' },
    findings: { type: 'array', maxItems: 10, items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'staleness, contradictions, overlaps, undiscoverable rules — with file:line-ish evidence' },
    simplifications: { type: 'array', maxItems: 8, items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'concrete cuts/merges that preserve safety' },
    updates: { type: 'array', maxItems: 8, items: { type: 'object', required: ['target', 'change', 'why'], properties: { target: { type: 'string' }, change: { type: 'string' }, why: { type: 'string' } } } },
    keep: { type: 'array', maxItems: 5, items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'load-bearing parts that must not be weakened' },
  },
}

function chunk(arr, n) {
  const out = []
  for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i += n) out.push(arr.slice(i, i + n))
  return out
}

function base(p) { return p.split('/').pop() }

function sessionPrompt(dir, machine) {
  const origin = machine === 'mini'
    ? 'This dir was rsynced from mini:~/orbit/.orbit/sessions/ — treat the basename as the original archive name; absolute paths inside artifacts refer to mini (/Users/nckrtl on mini), so they will not resolve here — judge them as written.'
    : 'This is a local archive under /Users/nckrtl/orbit/.orbit/sessions/.'
  return [
    CONTEXT,
    'You are analyzing ONE archived Orbit feature-loop session directory: ' + dir,
    origin,
    'Steps: (1) ls -R the directory (it is small). (2) Read loop.md fully. (3) Read evidence/ files — small ones fully, large ones via head/tail/grep. (4) ls quality-gates/ and read 1-2 representative artifacts (head -50). (5) Read agent-sessions/manifest.json if present.',
    'Reference the intended packet shape in /Users/nckrtl/orbit/LOOP.md.example (read it) — this file is on the local machine and applies to both machines.',
    'Judge: archive-name contract compliance for basename "' + base(dir) + '"; loop.md completeness vs the template; whether Final Distillation is genuine insight or boilerplate; whether candidate signals were captured during work or reconstructed; whether required-verification rows are honest; ceremony that visibly cost effort without payoff; dangling evidence pointers; whether agent-sessions transcripts were archived; friction recorded in Progress/Blockers; and improvement ideas for the loop itself.',
    STYLE,
  ].join('\n\n')
}

function codexPrompt(files, machine) {
  return [
    CONTEXT,
    'You are analyzing Codex CLI rollout transcript(s) from ' + machine + ' (feature-orchestrator sessions, last 5 days):\n' + files.join('\n'),
    'Files can be up to 40MB — NEVER read one fully. Recipe per file: head -c 3000 to learn the JSONL line schema; wc -l; then extract user and assistant MESSAGE TEXT with jq (adapt to the actual schema you saw, e.g. select on .type/.payload.type=="message" and join .content[].text); cap output with head. Also grep -c occurrences of markers: loop.md, Final Distillation, orbit-feature-finalization-check, orbit-prepare-worktree, orbit-session-archive, CHECKOUT_PROOF, spawn_agent, harness-signals, retained topology, quality-check, "is_error", failed. Then read the first ~10 and last ~30 extracted messages plus targeted grep windows (grep -n -m5 with context) around interesting markers.',
    'Determine: was this an Orbit implementation/orchestration cycle (cwd ~/orbit or a .worktrees path)? What task? Where did the agent stall, retry, or get confused? Did the finalization gate or archive naming block or confuse it? How much of the session was loop bookkeeping (loop.md editing, distillation, archiving, signal classification) vs implementation? What did the human have to correct? What instruction, doc, or tool wrinkle caused each friction?',
    STYLE,
  ].join('\n\n')
}

function claudePrompt(files, machine) {
  return [
    CONTEXT,
    'You are analyzing Claude Code session transcript(s) (JSONL) from ' + machine + ' (last 5 days):\n' + files.join('\n'),
    'These were typically Solo-spawned documenter/reviewer/post-feature-analyzer lanes or interactive orbit sessions. Recipe per file: head -c 3000 to learn the schema; extract user turns: jq -r with select(.type=="user") over .message.content (string or array of blocks — take .text of text blocks; note tool_result blocks); extract assistant text similarly; count tool errors with grep -c on is_error true patterns; look at first user message (the prompt/persona given) and the final assistant message (the verdict/report). Cap all output with head.',
    'Determine: which lane was this (implementer, documenter, reviewer persona, post-feature analyzer, interactive)? Did the CHECKOUT_PROOF requirement work or cause friction? Was the persona prompt oversized or contradictory? Did the agent produce a useful verdict or drift? What friction appeared (permission prompts, wrong cwd, missing tools, model unavailability, confusion about which doc rules)? How much was ceremony vs value?',
    STYLE,
  ].join('\n\n')
}

function grokPrompt(dirs, machine, note) {
  return [
    CONTEXT,
    'You are analyzing Grok CLI session dir(s) from ' + machine + ' (Grok is the default Solo implementation worker):\n' + dirs.join('\n'),
    note,
    'Recipe per session dir: read summary.json and signals.json if present; sample chat_history.jsonl / messages.jsonl (first user prompt fully — it is the worker handoff prompt shape from implementing-features SKILL; then last ~20 messages); ls terminal/ and head one log if informative. Cap output with head.',
    'Determine: what slice was assigned; did the worker prove pwd/branch first; did it follow TDD/first-narrow-diff rules or stall in discovery; did it need corrections; was the giant handoff prompt effective or noisy; friction with Solo/worktree/verification; improvement ideas for the worker handoff prompt shape.',
    STYLE,
  ].join('\n\n')
}

function skillPrompt(lane, paths, questions) {
  return [
    CONTEXT,
    'You are reviewing the "' + lane + '" lane of the Orbit loop harness. Read fully: ' + paths.join(', ') + '.',
    'Also read /Users/nckrtl/orbit/HARNESS.md and /Users/nckrtl/orbit/LOOP.md.example for cross-reference (skim for the relevant sections).',
    questions,
    'Evaluate: internal contradictions; contradictions with HARNESS.md; duplicated policy that should live in exactly one place; rules a fresh agent would misread or never discover; length vs value (what could be cut or turned into a checklist/tool); staleness vs the repo as it exists today (verify referenced files/commands exist with ls/rg); and what is load-bearing and must not be weakened.',
    STYLE,
  ].join('\n\n')
}

const S = args

phase('Sessions')
const sessionThunks = []
for (const d of S.localSessions) sessionThunks.push(() => agent(sessionPrompt(d, 'local'), { label: 'session:' + base(d), phase: 'Sessions', schema: SESSION_SCHEMA, effort: 'medium' }))
for (const d of S.miniSessions) sessionThunks.push(() => agent(sessionPrompt(d, 'mini'), { label: 'session:mini:' + base(d), phase: 'Sessions', schema: SESSION_SCHEMA, effort: 'medium' }))

const transcriptThunks = []
for (const grp of chunk(S.codexLocal, 2)) transcriptThunks.push(() => agent(codexPrompt(grp, 'local'), { label: 'codex:' + base(grp[0]).slice(8, 27), phase: 'Transcripts', schema: TRANSCRIPT_SCHEMA, effort: 'medium' }))
for (const grp of chunk(S.codexMini, 2)) transcriptThunks.push(() => agent(codexPrompt(grp, 'mini'), { label: 'codex:mini:' + base(grp[0]).slice(8, 27), phase: 'Transcripts', schema: TRANSCRIPT_SCHEMA, effort: 'medium' }))
for (const grp of chunk(S.claudeLocal, 4)) transcriptThunks.push(() => agent(claudePrompt(grp, 'local'), { label: 'claude:' + base(grp[0]).slice(0, 8), phase: 'Transcripts', schema: TRANSCRIPT_SCHEMA, effort: 'medium' }))
for (const grp of chunk(S.claudeMini, 4)) transcriptThunks.push(() => agent(claudePrompt(grp, 'mini'), { label: 'claude:mini:' + base(grp[0]).slice(0, 8), phase: 'Transcripts', schema: TRANSCRIPT_SCHEMA, effort: 'medium' }))
for (const grp of chunk(S.grokLocal, 3)) transcriptThunks.push(() => agent(grokPrompt(grp, 'local', 'Each path is one Grok session directory.'), { label: 'grok:' + base(grp[0]).slice(0, 13), phase: 'Transcripts', schema: TRANSCRIPT_SCHEMA, effort: 'medium' }))
for (const grp of chunk(S.grokMini, 2)) transcriptThunks.push(() => agent(grokPrompt(grp, 'mini', 'Each path is a PROJECT directory rsynced from mini that may contain one or more session subdirectories (UUID names) — analyze each session subdir inside; the URL-encoded dir name tells you the original cwd (worktree) on mini.'), { label: 'grok:mini:' + decodeURIComponent(base(grp[0])).split('/').pop(), phase: 'Transcripts', schema: TRANSCRIPT_SCHEMA, effort: 'medium' }))

const R = '/Users/nckrtl/orbit'
const skillLanes = [
  ['implementing-features', [R + '/.agents/skills/implementing-features/SKILL.md'], 'This is the central loop skill at 1165 lines. Pay special attention to: how much duplicates HARNESS.md/LOOP.md.example verbatim-ish; whether the 28-step Workflow is followable; whether prompt templates are too long to survive real handoffs; what could become executable tooling instead of prose; propose a concrete restructuring (target size, section split).'],
  ['root-docs-coherence', [R + '/AGENTS.md', R + '/HARNESS.md', R + '/AGENT_FAST_PATH.md', R + '/HARNESS_SIGNALS.md', R + '/harness-signals/README.md', R + '/CLAUDE.md'], 'Map duplication and contradictions across these root harness docs (archive-naming rules, merge gate, parallelization gate, search hygiene each appear in several places). Recommend a single-source-of-truth layout and what each doc should shrink to.'],
  ['bin-helpers', [R + '/bin/orbit-session-archive', R + '/bin/orbit-agent-session-archive', R + '/bin/orbit-feature-finalization-check', R + '/bin/orbit-prepare-worktree'], 'These are shell/PHP helpers enforcing the loop. Read each fully. Check: does orbit-session-archive GENERATE the compliant YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS name or trust the caller (real archives on both machines violate the naming contract — e.g. 20260701T112409Z-orbit-laravel-vite-env, 20260626171601-linked-test-lane-c)? Silent failure paths? Could more prose rules (naming, archive completeness, verification rows) move into these tools? Note UX wrinkles for agents invoking them.'],
  ['handling-feature-requests', [R + '/.agents/skills/handling-feature-requests/SKILL.md'], 'Intake-only skill. Check boundary clarity with implementing-features, scratchpad pre-dispatch gate ergonomics, and whether the intake-to-implementation handoff loses information.'],
  ['loop-observer+solo-todo-handoff', [R + '/.agents/skills/loop-observer/SKILL.md', R + '/.agents/skills/solo-todo-handoff/SKILL.md'], 'Self-improvement ingredients. Is loop-observer actually runnable/used? Does solo-todo-handoff still match the thin-CLI/Solo model? What would make observation lower-friction?'],
  ['quality-gate-triage', [R + '/.agents/skills/quality-gate-triage/SKILL.md'], 'Check lane map accuracy vs apps/docs/content/testing/README.md (skim it), artifact paths vs real .orbit/quality-gates contents, and classification-first discipline ergonomics.'],
  ['release', [R + '/.agents/skills/release/SKILL.md'], 'Check gate ordering, approval boundaries, doctor before/after flow, and overlap with HARNESS.md merge boundaries; look for steps that could be one command.'],
  ['command-designer', [R + '/.agents/skills/command-designer/SKILL.md'], 'Check whether it matches the current CLI contract surface and the retained-ingress-VM gate in implementing-features; flag overlap and gaps.'],
  ['evals-cluster', [R + '/.agents/skills/orbit-evals/SKILL.md', R + '/.agents/skills/construct-eval/SKILL.md', R + '/.agents/skills/execute-eval/SKILL.md', R + '/.agents/skills/evaluate-eval-execution/SKILL.md'], 'The eval self-improvement pipeline. Is the construct->execute->evaluate flow wired to session archives as HARNESS.md hints (eval wiring "remains a later slice")? What is the smallest next slice to make session archives feed evals?'],
  ['docs-cluster', [R + '/.agents/skills/updating-documentation/SKILL.md', R + '/.agents/skills/auditing-docs-drift/SKILL.md', R + '/.agents/skills/librarian/SKILL.md'], 'Docs lanes. Check role separation (routine update vs drift audit vs librarian tooling), overlap, and whether docs-first ordering guidance matches implementing-features.'],
  ['verification-cluster', [R + '/.agents/skills/e2e-verification-lanes/SKILL.md', R + '/.agents/skills/cli-output-pty-capture/SKILL.md'], 'Verification support lanes. Check consistency with the manual-only E2E rule, retained topology proof flow, and PTY-capture ergonomics; flag anything an agent could trip on.'],
  ['review-personas', [R + '/.agents/review-personas/cli-command.md', R + '/.agents/review-personas/docs-librarian.md', R + '/.agents/review-personas/post-feature-analyzer.md', R + '/.agents/review-personas/post-feature-distillation.md'], 'The review/self-improvement personas. Check size, prompt ergonomics for Solo-spawned Claude Opus, CHECKOUT_PROOF flow, overlap between post-feature-analyzer and post-feature-distillation, and verdict-shape clarity.'],
  ['harness-signals-ledger', [R + '/harness-signals/README.md', R + '/harness-signals/index.json', R + '/harness-signals/_template.md'], 'Also ls harness-signals/ and read 4-5 recent records. Judge: is the ledger being curated or accreting; are records discoverable/actionable; does index.json stay in sync; propose the smallest mechanism to keep signal quality high.'],
]

phase('Skills')
const skillThunks = skillLanes.map(([lane, paths, q]) => () => agent(skillPrompt(lane, paths, q), { label: 'skill:' + lane, phase: 'Skills', schema: SKILL_SCHEMA, effort: 'high' }))

log('Dispatching ' + sessionThunks.length + ' session analysts, ' + transcriptThunks.length + ' transcript analysts, ' + skillThunks.length + ' skill reviewers')

const pSessions = parallel(sessionThunks)
const pTranscripts = parallel(transcriptThunks)
const pSkills = parallel(skillThunks)
const sessions = await pSessions
const transcripts = await pTranscripts
const skills = await pSkills

const dropped = {
  sessions: sessions.filter(x => !x).length,
  transcripts: transcripts.filter(x => !x).length,
  skills: skills.filter(x => !x).length,
}
log('Done. Dropped (null) results: ' + JSON.stringify(dropped))

return { sessions: sessions.filter(Boolean), transcripts: transcripts.filter(Boolean), skills: skills.filter(Boolean), dropped }

# Orbit Harness Signals

This file maps repo-development signals to durable guardrail targets. It is a
routing table, not a changelog. Do not append every session event here; update
it only when Orbit learns a new class of signal or changes where that signal
should become guidance or enforcement.

## Signal Map

| Signal Source | Capture | Triage Question | Default Guardrail Target | Verification |
|---------------|---------|-----------------|--------------------------|--------------|
| Human review comment | Exact comment and affected files | Is this likely to recur across agents or slices? | `.agents/skills/**`, `HARNESS.md`, or tests | Re-read the changed route and run the narrowest relevant check. |
| Failed Pest, Mago, Rector, or docs-lint run | Command and failure excerpt | Is the failure message enough for the next agent to self-correct? | Test assertion message, skill runbook, or static rule | Re-run the failing command. |
| E2E or retained-topology failure | Topology id, role, command, and observed output | Is this a product bug, verification-lane gap, or missing setup guidance? | `apps/docs/content/testing/**`, `e2e-verification-lanes`, product docs, or E2E coverage | Re-run the focused lane or retained check. |
| Live-node bug report | Node, version, command, and before/after evidence | Is the repo correct but the installed/runtime surface stale? | Runtime-user verification rule, release skill, product docs, or regression test | Verify against the actual runtime user or live node. |
| Docs drift audit finding | Finding id, conflicting files, and authority chain | Is authority unclear, is one downstream doc stale, or is reviewer scope too broad? | `.agents/review-personas/docs-librarian.md`, product docs, product-decision ledger, banned term, or `auditing-docs-drift` | `composer docs-lint` and focused drift re-check. |
| Agent implementation mistake | Prompt, changed files, and correction needed | Did the agent miss routing, ownership, or verification context? | `AGENTS.md`, `HARNESS.md`, `LOOP.md`, or relevant skill | Run through the discovery path and confirm the missing route exists. |
| Worktree/bootstrap failure | Worktree path, command, and setup output | Is the setup flow broken or did an agent bypass it? | `bin/orbit-prepare-worktree`, `AGENTS.md`, or `implementing-features` | Prepare a fresh worktree or re-run the failed setup step. |
| Command-contract drift | Command, docs path, test path, and observed output | Is the public contract wrong, under-tested, missing reviewer coverage, or just the implementation stale? | `command-designer`, `.agents/review-personas/cli-command.md`, command docs, Pest coverage, or product-decision ledger | Focused Pest for the command plus docs-lint when docs changed. |
| Security or secret-handling concern | Affected surface and exposure path | Is this a concrete leak, missing review rule, or product policy change? | `spatie-security`, tests/static checks, product docs, or banned term | Focused security regression and relevant quality gate. |

## Guardrail Target Selection

- Treat raw `.orbit` artifacts, persisted `.orbit/sessions/` archives, session
  transcripts, scratchpads, and reviewer comments as candidate signals only.
  They do not become durable guardrails until the post-feature analyzer reviews the completed loop and the orchestrator adjudicates that recommendation against session context.
  Session archives are trace evidence for post-feature analysis and future eval
  construction; `harness-signals/` remains curated distilled learning and
  guardrail history, not raw session storage.
- Promote a candidate only when all of these are true:
  - A concrete mistake, late catch, expensive diagnosis, or high-risk near miss
    happened.
  - The same class of mistake is likely to recur across future features,
    worktrees, or agents.
  - Existing harness docs, skills, personas, tests, failure messages, and signal
    records did not already cover it clearly enough.
  - The proposed guardrail would likely have prevented the exact mistake or
    caught it earlier.
  - The smallest useful guardrail target is clear.
  - A narrow verification can prove the new target is reachable.
- Eliminate non-signals before considering promotion:
  - one-off handoffs or machine moves
  - lessons already covered by current code, tests, docs, skills, personas,
    signal records, static checks, or failure messages
  - reviewer findings fixed before merge when reviewer guidance already caught
    the issue
  - stale historical `.orbit/` artifacts that do not reveal a current gap
  - ordinary feature work that belongs in the active diff, not the harness
- Reject or mark `already-covered` when any promotion condition is missing.
  A final review that creates no durable guardrail is a valid loop result.
- Search `harness-signals/index.json` and then matching `harness-signals/`
  records before treating a durable signal as new. If a related signal is
  already `guarded` and the issue reappears, mark or treat the signal as
  `recurring` and evaluate whether the guardrail target needs to be tightened.
- Also check whether a later slice already absorbed the lesson in current code,
  tests, product or harness docs, skills, personas, static checks, or command
  failure messages. If it did, classify the candidate as `already-covered` and
  name the durable coverage instead of creating a duplicate record.
- Fix only the current diff when the signal is local and unlikely to recur.
- Create or update a `harness-signals/` record when the signal should remain
  searchable across worktrees. Do not copy raw session archives from
  `.orbit/sessions/` into `harness-signals/`; distill the lesson into a curated
  record instead.
- Update a skill when the signal is about workflow, command usage, ownership,
  verification, or environment setup.
- Update a reviewer persona when the signal is about post-test review criteria,
  evidence interpretation, or repeated mistakes that a focused review checklist
  should catch.
- Update the Solo role matrix or implementation skill when the signal is about
  which agent should own orchestration, documentation, implementation,
  verification, or review.
- Update product docs when the signal changes or clarifies user-facing Orbit
  behavior.
- Update tests or static checks when a future failure can be detected
  mechanically.
- Update root harness docs when the signal changes repo-wide discovery,
  feedback-loop routing, or the boundary between harness and product docs.
- Add a product-decision entry only for direction changes or reversals, not
  routine clarification.

## Minimum Evidence

Every distilled signal needs evidence that the chosen guardrail target works:

- Signal-ledger target: a searchable record under `harness-signals/` links the
  source, recurrence status, guardrail target, and verification.
- Documentation target: `git diff --check` and, when product docs changed,
  `composer docs-lint`.
- Skill target: read the skill from the root discovery path and confirm the new
  trigger or step is reachable.
- Test/static target: show the focused command failing before the fix when
  practical, then passing after.
- E2E/live target: record the exact lane, topology, node, command, and observed
  result.

Required E2E that cannot be completed is first a `blocked` feature-loop
outcome, not a candidate signal. Promote it only when the cause reveals a
recurring verification-lane, setup, or process gap.

## Current Manual Cadence

Run the loop during implementation handoff and final reporting. Periodic
distillation over CI, Solo todos, and review comments is intentionally deferred
until a later automation slice proves the manual guardrail-target map is stable.
Broad history or worktree mining is separate from the regular feature loop and
should run only when explicitly requested.

1	---
2	name: handling-feature-requests
3	description: Use when receiving, refining, triaging, or preparing an Orbit feature request, product change, command behavior change, scope question, or Solo todo handoff.
4	---
5	
6	# Handling Feature Requests
7	
8	## Overview
9	
10	Capture feature intent as a scoped handoff. This skill is intake-only: it does
11	not update files, documentation, tests, or implementation code.
12	
13	Before refining intent, use the `brainstorming` superpower for product shaping
14	or behavior changes. Once intent is clear, use this skill to decide whether the
15	request is one implementation slice or a larger feature that needs a lightweight
16	Solo scratchpad roadmap. Actual work, including documentation updates, happens
17	through the `implementing-features` skill.
18	
19	## Workflow
20	
21	1. Restate the requested outcome in concrete Orbit terms.
22	2. Identify the affected product surface: command, service, API, docs-only behavior, orchestration flow, E2E lane, or project tooling.
23	3. Use the `brainstorming` superpower when intent, behavior, scope, or product
24	   direction still needs refinement.
25	4. Read current product authority before writing the handoff:
26	   - `AGENTS.md`
27	   - `PRODUCT_DECISIONS.md` (dated intent ledger — read current direction before proposing a change, so a new decision does not contradict or duplicate an existing one)
28	   - `apps/docs/content/mission.md`
29	   - `apps/docs/content/architecture.md`
30	   - `apps/docs/content/tech-stack.md`
31	   - `apps/docs/content/concepts.md`
32	   - relevant `apps/docs/content/domains/**`
33	   - relevant `docs/superpowers/**`
34	5. Flag missing or contradictory docs in the handoff; do not fix them in
35	   this skill.
36	6. Define the smallest useful vertical slice that can be documented, tested,
37	   implemented, and verified. If the request is larger than one slice, create or
38	   update one lightweight Solo scratchpad with rough slice order, dependencies,
39	   slice outcomes, open decisions, and the final verification gate.
40	7. Create Solo todo(s) only when a slice needs asynchronous assignment, queueing,
41	   or explicit tracking outside the active orchestrator thread. If no todo is
42	   needed, the scratchpad or conversation handoff is enough.
43	8. Leave implementation, including documentation edits and product-decision
44	   ledger entries, to the agent using `implementing-features`.
45	
46	## Product Decisions
47	
48	Use this decision order when evidence conflicts:
49	
50	1. Current docs are product authority.
51	2. Current tests describe expected implementation behavior only when they match the docs.
52	3. Current code explains what exists, not necessarily what should exist.
53	
54	If a new decision is needed, make it explicit in the handoff:
55	
56	```markdown
57	Decision needed: <question>
58	Known evidence:
59	- Current docs: <path and summary>
60	- Current code/tests: <path and summary>
61	Recommended direction: <specific choice and why>
62	```
63	
64	## Handoff Shape
65	
66	Use this shape when creating a slice handoff in a scratchpad, conversation, or
67	Solo todo:
68	
69	```markdown
70	## Feature Request
71	<one-paragraph outcome>
72	
73	## Product Contract
74	- Authority docs:
75	- Behavior to add/change:
76	- Behavior explicitly out of scope:
77	- Existing code/test evidence:
78	
79	## Acceptance Criteria
80	- <observable behavior>
81	- <observable behavior>
82	
83	## Implementation Scope
84	- Owned files/domains:
85	- Foreign scope to avoid:
86	- Data or migration impact:
87	
88	## Test Plan
89	- New/changed tests:
90	- Focused verification command:
91	- Broader verification command, if needed:
92	- E2E/live-node lane:
93	
94	## Risks
95	- <risk or none>
96	```
97	
98	## Solo Delegation Rules
99	
100	- This skill may create or update Solo scratchpads, todos, comments, blockers,
101	  and tags.
102	- This skill must not edit repository files or spawn implementation agents.
103	- Documentation updates, product-decision ledger entries, tests, and code
104	  changes all belong to a later implementation pass using
105	  `implementing-features`.
106	- The scratchpad is the feature roadmap when multiple slices are needed. Solo
107	  todos are optional assignment cards; keep them thin and point to the
108	  scratchpad plus the named slice instead of duplicating the full loop contract.
109	- Include enough context for a later implementation agent to start the slice
110	  without reconstructing intent from the conversation.
111	- Active `.orbit/` is worktree-local session state. Completed active state
112	  should be archived into the persistent project archive home before worktree
113	  cleanup and before rewriting `.orbit/loop.md` for a new slice. The default
114	  archive home is the primary checkout's
115	  `.orbit/sessions/<timestamp-feature-slug>/`, named as
116	  `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<feature-slug>` in the checkout's local time. Do not use
117	  compact timestamps, `T` separators, `Z`, or UTC offsets in archive directory
118	  names. Archives preserve every active `.orbit/` entry except
119	  `.orbit/sessions/`, including `loop.md`, `.orbit/evidence/`,
120	  `.orbit/quality-gates/`, and future metadata or manifests when tooling
121	  exists. `harness-signals/` remains curated distilled learning, not raw
122	  session storage. Post-feature analysis and future eval construction may
123	  inspect session archives as trace evidence; archive helper scripts and eval

---
name: handling-feature-requests
description: Use when receiving, refining, triaging, or preparing an Orbit feature request, product change, command behavior change, scope question, or Solo todo handoff.
---

# Handling Feature Requests

## Overview

Capture feature intent as a scoped handoff. This skill is intake-only: it does
not update files, documentation, tests, or implementation code.

Before refining intent, use the `brainstorming` superpower for product shaping
or behavior changes. Once intent is clear, use this skill to decide whether the
request is one implementation slice or a larger feature that needs a lightweight
Solo scratchpad roadmap. Actual work, including documentation updates, happens
through the `implementing-features` skill.

## Workflow

1. Restate the requested outcome in concrete Orbit terms.
2. Identify the affected product surface: command, service, API, docs-only behavior, orchestration flow, E2E lane, or project tooling.
3. Use the `brainstorming` superpower when intent, behavior, scope, or product
   direction still needs refinement.
4. Read current product authority before writing the handoff:
   - `AGENTS.md`
   - `PRODUCT_DECISIONS.md` (dated intent ledger — read current direction before proposing a change, so a new decision does not contradict or duplicate an existing one)
   - `apps/docs/content/mission.md`
   - `apps/docs/content/architecture.md`
   - `apps/docs/content/tech-stack.md`
   - `apps/docs/content/concepts.md`
   - relevant `apps/docs/content/domains/**`
   - relevant `docs/superpowers/**`
5. Flag missing or contradictory docs in the handoff; do not fix them in
   this skill.
6. Define the smallest useful vertical slice that can be documented, tested,
   implemented, and verified. If the request is larger than one slice, create or
   update one lightweight Solo scratchpad with rough slice order, dependencies,
   slice outcomes, open decisions, and the final verification gate.
7. Create Solo todo(s) only when a slice needs asynchronous assignment, queueing,
   or explicit tracking outside the active orchestrator thread. If no todo is
   needed, the scratchpad or conversation handoff is enough.
8. Leave implementation, including documentation edits and product-decision
   ledger entries, to the agent using `implementing-features`.

## Product Decisions

Use this decision order when evidence conflicts:

1. Current docs are product authority.
2. Current tests describe expected implementation behavior only when they match the docs.
3. Current code explains what exists, not necessarily what should exist.

If a new decision is needed, make it explicit in the handoff:

```markdown
Decision needed: <question>
Known evidence:
- Current docs: <path and summary>
- Current code/tests: <path and summary>
Recommended direction: <specific choice and why>
```

## Handoff Shape

Use this shape when creating a slice handoff in a scratchpad, conversation, or
Solo todo:

```markdown
## Feature Request
<one-paragraph outcome>

## Product Contract
- Authority docs:
- Behavior to add/change:
- Behavior explicitly out of scope:
- Existing code/test evidence:

## Acceptance Criteria
- <observable behavior>
- <observable behavior>

## Implementation Scope
- Owned files/domains:
- Foreign scope to avoid:
- Data or migration impact:

## Test Plan
- New/changed tests:
- Focused verification command:
- Broader verification command, if needed:
- E2E/live-node lane:

## Risks
- <risk or none>
```

## Solo Delegation Rules

- This skill may create or update Solo scratchpads, todos, comments, blockers,
  and tags.
- This skill must not edit repository files or spawn implementation agents.
- Documentation updates, product-decision ledger entries, tests, and code
  changes all belong to a later implementation pass using
  `implementing-features`.
- The scratchpad is the feature roadmap when multiple slices are needed. Solo
  todos are optional assignment cards; keep them thin and point to the
  scratchpad plus the named slice instead of duplicating the full loop contract.
- Include enough context for a later implementation agent to start the slice
  without reconstructing intent from the conversation.
- Active `.orbit/` is worktree-local session state. Completed active state
  should be archived into the persistent project archive home before worktree
  cleanup and before rewriting `.orbit/loop.md` for a new slice. The default
  archive home is the primary checkout's
  `.orbit/sessions/<timestamp-feature-slug>/`, named as
  `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<feature-slug>` in the checkout's local time. Do not use
  compact timestamps, `T` separators, `Z`, or UTC offsets in archive directory
  names. Archives preserve every active `.orbit/` entry except
  `.orbit/sessions/`, including `loop.md`, `.orbit/evidence/`,
  `.orbit/quality-gates/`, and future metadata or manifests when tooling
  exists. `harness-signals/` remains curated distilled learning, not raw
  session storage. Post-feature analysis and future eval construction may
  inspect session archives as trace evidence; archive helper scripts and eval
  wiring are later slices.

## Implementation Handoff

```markdown
Use `.agents/skills/implementing-features/SKILL.md` when executing this slice.

Task:
<paste the implementation handoff>

Required context:
- `AGENTS.md`
- `PRODUCT_DECISIONS.md` (dated intent ledger — current direction)
- relevant product docs under `apps/docs/content/**`
- relevant session context under `docs/superpowers/**`
- current code and tests in owned scope

Return changed files, tests, verification, blockers, and risks.
```

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and ask for direction if current docs contradict the requested behavior.
- Stop and ask for direction if the request requires destructive live-node work without an ephemeral E2E plan.
- Stop and narrow scope if the request mixes unrelated product surfaces.
- Stop before editing repository files; switch to `implementing-features` for
  actual changes.
- Stop before spawning implementation agents; leave execution to the
  implementation workflow.

## Common Mistakes

- Treating an implementation guess as product authority.
- Editing docs, code, tests, or skills while using this intake skill.
- Creating Solo todos for every slice when a scratchpad plus active
  orchestrator thread is enough.
- Spawning an implementation agent instead of capturing the work in a scratchpad
  or handoff.
- Creating broad abstractions before the vertical slice proves they are needed.
- Splitting documentation into a separate implementation track instead of
  capturing the doc gap in the handoff for `implementing-features`.

<result># Cross-provider friction themes (45 transcript groups; counts = groups exhibiting theme)

**1. Mandated-reading / onboarding ceremony — ~20 groups.** All providers; worst for grok workers and claude reviewer/analyzer lanes; codex orchestrators too. Prompts list 8–15 docs for tiny diffs; Grok additionally injects 60–72KB boilerplate around 3–5KB handoffs. "36 of 75 commands read harness/skill docs before any work" (codex-agent-cli-tools); "~15 mandatory files pushed one worker to 86% context before verification finished" (codex-thread grok worker). **Fix:** per-slice read budgets and a condensed persona/harness digest; drop docs already injected (AGENTS.md) and scale required reading to diff size.

**2. Wrong checkout / path resolution — ~16 groups.** All providers. apply_patch/loop.md land in the primary checkout ("apply_patch has no workdir"), Solo-spawned lanes start in ~/orbit not the worktree, relative `.orbit/loop.md` reads fail, `bin/orbit-gateway-pest` rejects root-relative paths. "The orchestration patch tool had no workdir... worker blocked twice on missing loop.md" (dependency-audit); "Solo-spawned Claude agents start in root checkout, not assigned worktree" (codex-thread). **Fix:** spawn with cwd pinned to the worktree, `bin/orbit-prepare-worktree` seeds `.orbit/loop.md`, absolute paths in every dispatch prompt, wrappers accept both path forms.

**3. Lost / dead lanes and transcript loss — ~15 groups.** Mostly claude lanes; also grok DOA spawns. Analyzers/reviewers die mid-run with no verdict; title-only empty sessions; capture-and-delete run in parallel destroys transcripts. "Output capture and process delete were issued in parallel — destroyed worker/analyzer transcripts three times in one loop" (AGENT_FAST_PATH analyzer); "92a7a88f ends mid-review after 4 tool calls/14s, no verdict, no error entry" (format-roots review). **Fix:** enforce capture→verify→delete sequencing in spawn tooling; require incremental findings written to `.orbit/evidence/`; detect zero-output spawns and auto-respawn.

**4. Solo MCP identity/tooling friction — ~12 groups.** codex + claude + grok. whoami/identify_session not exposed, `solo_api_not_configured`, transport drops, scratchpad schema guesses, unused "call whoami() first" boilerplate in lanes that never touch Solo. "solo_mini MCP handle just dropped with Transport closed" (agent-cli-tools); "Opus guessed wrong 4 times" on scratchpad_append_section params (codex-thread docs lane). **Fix:** inject SOLO_PROCESS_ID / auto-register external actors; make the Solo preamble conditional on lanes that actually use it; document scratchpad schemas with example calls.

**5. Worker discipline: over-exploration, skipped TDD/proof — ~11 groups.** Mostly grok workers; codex-spawned workers too. Discovery stalls needing interrupts, proof printed after edits, tests written after code, placeholder tests. "Worker 683 was stopped with no file changes after over-exploration" (extension CLI); "stop researching now and report a concise final table" (agent-cli-tools verifier, 29 web searches). **Fix:** CHECKOUT_PROOF as literal first output gated within N tool calls; explicit inspection budgets ("write outcome after 8–12 commands") in first dispatch, not retry.

**6. Finalization/merge-gate churn — ~10 groups.** Almost exclusively codex orchestrators. Gate rejects prose ("needs the literal value complete"), any angle-bracket token, stale docs-lint artifacts after every amend; retained-topology proof demanded for formatting/docs-only diffs. "~6 reruns... packet still had complete for..." (agent-cli-tools); "it rejected my ambiguous 'complete pending...' wording" (git-tool). **Fix:** finalization-check dry-run/lint mode at first checkpoint with exact failing token; auto-refresh docs-lint at HEAD; N/A classification for non-topology diffs.

**7. Analyzer/reviewer dispatched before preconditions — ~9 groups.** claude lanes flag it, codex causes it: uncommitted diffs (`git log main..HEAD` empty), Final Distillation still "pending" at analyzer time. "No commit / empty branch diff (HEAD == base)" (agent-cli-tools analyzer). **Fix:** gate analyzer dispatch on committed branch + filled distillation.

**8. Silent long gates / polling burn — ~9 groups.** codex orchestrators. quality-check, update:all, doctor emit nothing for minutes; reviewer completion has no signal. "~27 get_process_output calls every 3–5s" (solo-extension); "Still no doctor verdict after another interval" (git-tool). **Fix:** heartbeat/stream output for gates; blocking wait primitive keyed on checkpoint markers.

**9. Handoff contract gaps — ~9 groups.** grok workers mostly. Missing test entrypoints, API shapes, env facts, exact MCP tool names cause wrong guesses and correction rounds. "Could not open input file: artisan" (skill:install); "Tool not found: qmd-orbit__search" (codex-thread). **Fix:** handoff template with exact runner commands, tool names, env absences, inline API contracts.

**10. Green-but-broken-live / fake-only proof — ~8 groups.** codex + claude flags. Synthetic fixtures pass while live behavior fails; upstream Solo API shapes never verified. "Merged green on synthetic fixtures but broken live: 'I do not see the session files'" (session-archive); "five candidate rebuild/deploy cycles because gateway proxy contract mismatched real Solo API" (solo-extension). **Fix:** require one live-artifact/live-API verification before merging integration features.

**11. Toolchain drift / lint appeasement — ~8 groups.** Mago 1.41.0 vs pin 1.40.1 renoted by every lane; cli_rector `#[\Override]` drift blocked two merges; complexity-threshold refactors "just to pass lint" (~10 iterations, empty-json-meta). **Fix:** pin/sync binaries at worktree prep; scheduled main Rector sweep.

**12. Duplicate/conflicting reviewers — ~7 groups.** codex dispatch, claude lanes. "A 'NEEDS_WORK' at 20:06, B 'CLEAN' at 20:08" on the identical diff (solo-extension). **Fix:** idempotent reviewer dispatch via locks; reconciliation rule for conflicting verdicts; machine-parseable final verdict block.

**13. Archive naming/skipped archiving — ~6 groups.** codex. Forbidden compact T/Z timestamps; `bin/orbit-session-archive` never invoked (grep 0 across sessions). **Fix:** make the script the only archive path and have it enforce naming.

## (a) Ceremony share — codex orchestrators

Codex orchestrator sessions spend roughly **25–70% (median ~45%)** of turns on loop bookkeeping — loop.md packets, gate reruns, archives, and above all waiting/polling — vs implementation. Strongest data points:
- "~188 of 510 assistant messages are waiting/polling for Mini worker checkpoints" (agent-cli-tools, 50–60% ceremony).
- "60–70%... ~50 were polling reviewer/analyzer, ~40 quality-check reruns/flake triage" incl. "Still no report. I'm holding the line" (git-tool loop).
- "~95% of unit 08-33-47: only edits were loop.md create/delete/recreate plus checkpoint writes, zero implementation" (codex-thread bootstrap).

## (b) Most common user corrections

- **"Actually finish it":** agents stop before integrating/verifying — "Make sure it gets merged", "OK, commit and merge", "changes always have to be merged back into main".
- **"It doesn't actually work":** users catch green-but-broken output — "I do not see the session files", "Hey, but that's not the latest git version", "Please verify it in the browser. This is now the fifth time".
- **Tool/venue/flag redirects:** "You need to use Orbit", "just use the raw solo MCP", "use --stream-json", "address this in the main branch" — wrong tool or wrong layer chosen despite documentation.

## (c) Per-provider patterns

- **codex (orchestrators):** carry nearly all gate/merge/archival ceremony and worker-babysitting cost; failure mode is process churn (polling, gate literalism, cross-machine handoffs), not bad code; often end up doing the work themselves after worker failure.
- **claude (reviewer/documenter/analyzer):** individually lean (15–35% ceremony) and catch real bugs (parser bugs, dead API surface, doc drift), but lane *reliability* is the weak point — stalls, deaths without verdicts, empty spawns, verdict-format drift.
- **grok (workers):** fast, compact TDD once anchored (slices in ~2 min), but bimodal: over-exploration stalls vs clean runs; skip proof/TDD ordering; orchestrator interrupts frequently arrive stale after the worker already finished; buried under 60–72KB injected boilerplate.

## (d) One-off findings too important to drop

1. **librarian:build destroys content non-atomically** — "unintentionally collapsed apps/docs/content/concepts.md to a header before failing"; also rewrote it to the vendor skeleton in another loop.
2. **Config-reachable gate bypass** — implementer set `generated_docs.enforce=false`, making a green quality-check "partially hollow"; only a reviewer noticed.
3. **Poisoned durable memory** — loop.md distillation "inverted the shipped datatable contract; a future agent reading it would implement the rejected behavior".
4. **Silent wrong-subset green** — Pest "Option --filter cannot be used more than once" warning silently ran the wrong tests yet reported passed; plus parallel pest runs race on the shared mutate cache.
5. **Friction telemetry undercounts** — Grok signals.json reported `toolFailureCount:0` despite exit-code-2 failures, so loop telemetry misses real friction.</result>

## (a) Ceremony share — codex orchestrators

Codex orchestrator sessions spend roughly **25–70% (median ~45%)** of turns on loop bookkeeping — loop.md packets, gate reruns, archives, and above all waiting/polling — vs implementation. Strongest data points:
- "~188 of 510 assistant messages are waiting/polling for Mini worker checkpoints" (agent-cli-tools, 50–60% ceremony).
- "60–70%... ~50 were polling reviewer/analyzer, ~40 quality-check reruns/flake triage" incl. "Still no report. I'm holding the line" (git-tool loop).
- "~95% of unit 08-33-47: only edits were loop.md create/delete/recreate plus checkpoint writes, zero implementation" (codex-thread bootstrap).

## (b) Most common user corrections

- **"Actually finish it":** agents stop before integrating/verifying — "Make sure it gets merged", "OK, commit and merge", "changes always have to be merged back into main".
- **"It doesn't actually work":** users catch green-but-broken output — "I do not see the session files", "Hey, but that's not the latest git version", "Please verify it in the browser. This is now the fifth time".
- **Tool/venue/flag redirects:** "You need to use Orbit", "just use the raw solo MCP", "use --stream-json", "address this in the main branch" — wrong tool or wrong layer chosen despite documentation.

## (c) Per-provider patterns

- **codex (orchestrators):** carry nearly all gate/merge/archival ceremony and worker-babysitting cost; failure mode is process churn (polling, gate literalism, cross-machine handoffs), not bad code; often end up doing the work themselves after worker failure.
- **claude (reviewer/documenter/analyzer):** individually lean (15–35% ceremony) and catch real bugs (parser bugs, dead API surface, doc drift), but lane *reliability* is the weak point — stalls, deaths without verdicts, empty spawns, verdict-format drift.
- **grok (workers):** fast, compact TDD once anchored (slices in ~2 min), but bimodal: over-exploration stalls vs clean runs; skip proof/TDD ordering; orchestrator interrupts frequently arrive stale after the worker already finished; buried under 60–72KB injected boilerplate.

input.content:
# Orbit Loop Review 2026-07-02 — Findings & Improvement Plan

## Scope and method

Every archived `.orbit/sessions/` session on both machines was analyzed: 12 on this Mac and 26 on mini (38/38, none skipped). On top of that, all Codex, Claude, and Grok agent transcripts from the last 5 days that backed implementation cycles were reviewed (32 Codex rollouts, 63 Claude session files, 29 Grok session dirs across both machines), plus a full review of the 13 loop-relevant harness lanes (implementing-features, handling-feature-requests, loop-observer, solo-todo-handoff, quality-gate-triage, release, command-designer, the eval cluster, the docs cluster, the verification cluster, review personas, harness-signals ledger, root harness docs, and the four `bin/` loop helpers). 96 analysis agents produced the raw findings; three synthesis passes clustered them. Raw clustered digests live in the session scratchpad dir (`findings-sessions.jsonl`, `findings-transcripts.jsonl`, `findings-skills.jsonl`).

## Headline numbers

- 26 of 38 session archives violate the mandated `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<slug>` naming contract — a rule restated 7 times across the docs and still broken in most real archives.
- 37 of 38 archives have no usable provider transcripts (`agent-sessions/` missing entirely, or present with 16-of-18 `missing` manifest stubs due to capture bugs: `codex_token_count_not_found`, `grok_signals_not_found`, `claude_session_pid_missing`).
- 37 of 38 archives contain evidence pointers that no longer resolve (dead Solo process ids, `/tmp` paths, empty `evidence/` dirs).
- 8 of 38 loop outcomes are free prose instead of the required `complete | blocked | complete + loop improvement` enum — and the finalization gate passed them anyway.
- Codex orchestrator sessions spend roughly 25–70% (median ~45%) of turns on loop bookkeeping and polling rather than implementation.
- Final Distillation content is genuinely reasoned in ~35 of 38 packets — the loop's reflective core works. The failures are mechanical: capture, naming, archiving, pointer integrity, and gate enforcement.

The overall read: **the loop's thinking is healthy, its plumbing is not.** Prose rules that tools could enforce are duplicated everywhere and violated anyway, while the tools that exist (`bin/orbit-session-archive`, `bin/orbit-feature-finalization-check`) are too lenient, not wired into the workflow steps, or silently bypassed.

## Top wrinkles (ranked by evidence volume)

### 1. Session archiving is the weakest link (37/38 sessions affected)
`bin/orbit-session-archive` either never ran or its provider capture silently failed everywhere. The four `dependency-audit-posture-v1` archives on mini are one feature loop archived four times in 8 minutes: the script has no idempotency/slug-dedup, mints UTC-derived basenames (naming says local time), and every finalization retry looked like a fresh session. Rename-after-archive leaves dead self-pointers in loop.md (e.g. `quality-check-progress-monotonic` points at a nonexistent compact-T-Z path).
**Fix (tool, not prose):** the script generates the basename itself in local time; validates `--archive-dir` against the contract; dedupes per feature slug (update, don't re-mint); writes the final archive path back into loop.md; copies `/tmp`-cited artifacts into `evidence/` and rewrites pointers archive-relative; fails loudly on missing loop.md, zero discovered sessions, or failed provider capture. Fix the three provider-capture bugs.

### 2. The finalization gate is too weak to protect its own contract (~23 sessions)
Free-prose outcomes, literal `pending` placeholders, missing template labels (`- Deferred follow-up:` singular instead of plural), analyzer rows relabeled from reviewers, and even `HEAD == base` with an empty branch diff all passed. The gate is also absent from the implementing-features 28-step workflow, and the hook exits 0 silently on unclassifiable input.
**Fix:** validate enums and label shapes; reject placeholder values; require the verified diff committed at HEAD; add an agent-sessions/manifest row; print explicit `PASS`/`BLOCKED` with the exact failing token; add a `--lint` dry-run mode agents can run at the first checkpoint instead of discovering failures through ~6 merge-time reruns; make the check an explicit numbered workflow step.

### 3. Ceremony scales with the template, not the change (~27 sessions; ~45% orchestrator overhead)
Single-slice loops fill the full start gate, parallelization scan, and analyzer scaffolding with `not applicable` boilerplate ("Full Parallelization scan filled out for a one-file Markdown edit"). One Codex bootstrap session was ~95% loop.md create/delete/recreate with zero implementation. Polling is the other half: ~188 of 510 orchestrator messages in one loop were wait-polling workers; ~27 `get_process_output` calls every 3–5s in another.
**Fix:** ship a compact single-slice loop.md variant (start gate + parallelization collapse to one `serial: <reason>` line); add a blocking wait/heartbeat primitive for gates and Solo workers (checkpoint markers instead of polling); add docs-only/skills-only gate profiles so a `.agents/skills/**` diff doesn't burn a 44s full quality-check.

### 4. Worker/reviewer dispatch is unreliable (22 sessions, ~15 transcript groups)
Wrong-cwd starts (Solo lanes open in `~/orbit` instead of the worktree; apply_patch has no workdir), first-diff stalls needing interrupts, DOA/empty spawns, analyzers dying mid-run with no verdict, and capture-vs-delete races that destroyed transcripts three times in one loop. Duplicate reviewers returned contradictory verdicts on the identical diff ("NEEDS_WORK" at 20:06, "CLEAN" at 20:08).
**Fix:** spawn tooling pins and mechanically verifies worktree cwd; `bin/orbit-prepare-worktree` seeds `.orbit/loop.md`; first-diff/health budgets stated in the first dispatch prompt ("write outcome after 8–12 commands"), not as a retry correction; a serialized capture→verify→delete helper replaces the prose rule; incremental reviewer findings stream to `.orbit/evidence/` so a dead lane still leaves a partial verdict; idempotent reviewer dispatch via locks plus a machine-parseable verdict block.

### 5. Onboarding/reading ceremony overloads workers (~20 transcript groups)
Prompts mandate 8–15 docs for tiny diffs; Grok workers get 60–72KB of injected boilerplate around 3–5KB handoffs; one worker hit 86% context before verification finished; 36 of 75 commands in one Codex session were harness-doc reads before any work.
**Fix:** scale required reading to diff size; provide a condensed harness digest for workers; drop docs already injected by the harness (AGENTS.md); keep the CHECKOUT_PROOF + first-narrow-diff rules (those work) but put read budgets in the handoff template.

### 6. Gate noise: flakes, pre-existing failures, stale baselines (16 sessions)
`cli_rector` Override drift blocked two merges; `E2ECurrentCheckoutTest` flaked post-merge; cold-worktree timing baselines produce false warnings; plain `composer quality-check` gets killed (exit 143) unless `ORBIT_QUALITY_CHECK_MAX_BACKGROUND_JOBS=40`; one "passed" artifact claims 5810 Pest tests in 29s (silently cached/short-circuited subgates). A silent Pest warning (`--filter cannot be used more than once`) ran the wrong test subset and still reported green.
**Fix:** first-class `pre_existing_unrelated` waiver artifact in the merge gate; quarantine/fix the known flake; seed cold-worktree baselines during prepare-worktree; make the background-jobs cap the script default; scheduled Rector sweep on main; treat runner warnings as failures in gate scripts.

### 7. Candidate signals are reconstructed, not captured (13 sessions)
`Candidate Signals While Working: none` coexists with a populated Final Distillation — exactly the reconstruction the template forbids. The signal ledger confirms it: all 29 harness-signals records were created in a 3-day window ending 2026-06-25; heavy work since produced zero records.
**Fix:** auto-seed candidate signals from nonzero-exit gate artifacts; flag `none` + non-empty distillation as a reconstruction smell in the finalization check; add `bin/orbit-harness-signal-index --check` (fail on nonexistent guardrail targets and stale `pending` markers) to docs-lint.

### 8. Green-but-broken-live (~8 transcript groups; top user-correction class)
Synthetic fixtures pass while live behavior fails ("I do not see the session files"; five candidate rebuild/deploy cycles because a proxy contract mismatched the real Solo API; "Please verify it in the browser. This is now the fifth time"). The other top corrections: "actually finish it — merge it back", and wrong-tool/wrong-layer redirects.
**Fix:** integration features require one live-artifact/live-API verification row before merge; deferred live proofs mint a Solo todo at finalization instead of being archived and forgotten (frankenphp-runtime-ca-trust lost its deferred live-node proofs this way).

## Doc/skill debt (from the 13-lane review)

### Duplication map (single-source-of-truth targets)
- Archive naming rule: 7 copies (HARNESS.md ×4, LOOP.md.example ×2, harness-signals/README) → move to the tool + one HARNESS.md sentence.
- Opus spawn recipe (`--model opus --effort medium`): 5 copies → live only in the HARNESS.md Solo Role Matrix; personas get a one-line pointer.
- Roadmap-mirroring policy: 5 copies; thin-todo rule: 5 copies; comparative-eval rules: 5 copies; parallelization gate / search hygiene / scratchpad pre-dispatch gate: 3 copies each with drifting wording.
- Keep the E2E manual-only rule's cross-doc redundancy — that one is intentional and load-bearing.

### Direct contradictions to resolve
1. Analyzer timing: implementing-features:322 says analyzer runs "before commit/merge-back"; HARNESS.md:407 says the audit happens "after merge". Pick one (HARNESS.md should win), state it once.
2. implementing-features:1049 says completed work is "cleaned up" vs HARNESS.md leave-worktree-until-audit.
3. solo-todo-handoff "never prepend anything before /goal" vs implementing-features:192 "prepend agent_instructions". Also: `/goal` is mandated but defined nowhere.
4. updating-documentation lists `docs/superpowers/**` as product authority; HARNESS.md:189/AGENTS.md:68 say it is not.
5. auditing-docs-drift step 9 applies fixes directly vs AGENTS.md worktree-only implementation.
6. handling-feature-requests decision order omits the PRODUCT_DECISIONS ledger tiebreaker that AGENTS.md puts on top; its handoff templates also have no `Feature roadmap scratchpad: <solo://…>` field, so the pre-dispatch gate's URL is silently dropped at handoff.
7. HARNESS.md:316 "no outer loop-improver watcher" contradicts the entire loop-observer skill (see self-improvement below).
8. quality-gate-triage:265 reads as spawning E2E workers vs the HARNESS.md ban.

### Staleness sweep (all fail or misroute a fresh agent today)
- implementing-features: root `vendor/bin/mago` and root `php artisan test` don't exist (no root vendor/ or artisan).
- librarian skill: `php artisan librarian:*` from root and `docs/README.md` spine — real path is `bin/orbit-docs-artisan` + `apps/docs/content/`.
- command-designer references mandate phantom code: `App\Data\CommandResponses\`, `respondWithSuccess/Data`, `WithSpinner`, wrong `WithStepTree` namespace — zero matches in apps/cli or its git history; agents currently write uncompilable code from these.
- cli-output-pty-capture: relative `scripts/capture_pty_frames.py` (no root scripts/); also has a near-verbatim duplicated section and uses fleet-mutating `orbit update:all` as its copy-paste example.
- harness-signals records: `composer e2e:incus` (real: `test:e2e:incus`), guardrail target `LOOP.md` (only LOOP.md.example exists), a "pending loop-hardening" commit that never existed.
- handling-feature-requests:123 + HARNESS.md:327 still call archive tooling "later slices" though `bin/orbit-session-archive` exists.
- release skill: split-repo list missing orbit-sdk-laravel; 120-line inline step-7 script with cross-step shell variables that don't survive agent shells → extract `bin/orbit-release-candidate` persisting build_id/digests to a state file.
- prepare-worktree composer loop omits apps/reverb; AGENTS.md misses packages/sdk + apps/e2e; `caller_role_not_allowed` documented with no emitter.

## Self-improvement pipeline: ingredients exist, pipes are broken

- **Capture stalled:** signal ledger frozen since 2026-06-25; lifecycle states unused; `pending` markers never resolve.
- **Analyzer stage lossy:** verdict vocabulary undefined (`mixed|blocked` appear in the wild), CHECKOUT_PROOF is defined only inside implementing-features so a Solo-spawned reviewer reading its persona never learns of it, post-feature-distillation.md is orphaned yet pinned by McpConfigurationTest prose assertions.
- **Observer stage dead:** loop-observer is referenced by nothing (not HARNESS.md, not the role matrix, not LOOP.md.example) and its premise is contradicted by HARNESS.md:316. Wire it in as an explicitly-requested observation lane with a trigger sentence in the role matrix, or delete it.
- **Archives don't feed evals:** no eval skill references `.orbit/sessions/`; `_orbit-eval-references/session-mining.md` mines raw `~/.codex/sessions` homedir files while the structured `agent-sessions/<provider>/*/messages.jsonl` + manifest archives sit unused.
- **Smallest wiring slice (docs-only, no new tooling):** add a "Session Archives" source section to session-mining.md preferring archive messages.jsonl/manifest over raw homedir files; add archive-slug as a valid `source:` provenance in eval-artifact-schema.md; broaden construct-eval's trigger; delete the stale "later slice" sentences (HARNESS.md:116/327).
- **Telemetry undercounts friction:** Grok signals.json reported `toolFailureCount: 0` despite exit-code-2 failures — live loop telemetry misses exactly the events the observer/analyzer stages need.
- **Poisoned memory hazard:** one loop.md distillation inverted the shipped datatable contract; a future agent reading it would implement the rejected behavior. Distillation packets need the same reviewer eye as code.

## What is working (do not weaken)

1. E2E manual-only rule (`composer test:e2e*` never agent-run) including its intentional redundancy.
2. The executable, artifact-backed merge gate concept (label-based Final Distillation + finalization check) — it needs teeth, not removal.
3. `bin/orbit-prepare-worktree` exclusivity with stop-and-report.
4. Human-approval boundaries: release keyed to build_id/digest, human-before-live-mutation.
5. No silent model downgrade; analyzer read-only boundary.
6. Eval integrity rules (answer-key/grader isolation).
7. Docs-first authority chain with PRODUCT_DECISIONS as dated tiebreaker.
8. Final Distillation as reflective practice — 35/38 packets show genuine reasoning; the CHECKOUT_PROOF and first-narrow-diff rules demonstrably anchor workers when applied.

## Suggested implementation order

1. **Harden `bin/orbit-session-archive`** (naming generation, `--archive-dir` validation, slug idempotency, pointer rewriting, /tmp artifact copy-in, loud failures, provider-capture fixes). Highest leverage: kills themes 1, 2, 5 and the mini quadruplicate-archive bug at the tool layer.

6. **Worker dispatch hardening** (cwd pinning, first-diff budgets, capture→verify→delete helper, streamed reviewer findings, read budgets, exact runner commands in handoffs).
7. **Gate noise reduction** (docs-only profile, waiver artifact, flake quarantine, background-jobs default, warning-as-failure).
8. **Wire archives → evals** (docs-only slice above) and decide loop-observer's fate; extract `bin/orbit-release-candidate`.

Done. The full review is complete and the improvement plan is written to Solo scratchpad **"Orbit Loop Review 2026-07-02 — Findings & Improvement Plan"** (id 223, orbit project, `solo://proj/4/scratchpad/orbit-loop-review-20--223`).

**Coverage:** all 38 `.orbit/sessions` archives analyzed — 12 on this Mac, 26 on mini (synced over SSH) — plus 32 Codex rollouts, 63 Claude session files, and 29 Grok session dirs from the last 5 days on both machines, plus all 13 loop-relevant skill/persona/doc/bin-helper lanes. 96 analysis agents, zero failures.

**The central finding:** the loop's *thinking* is healthy — ~35 of 38 Final Distillation packets contain genuine, well-reasoned insight. The loop's *plumbing* is what's broken, and prose rules haven't fixed it:

- **26/38 archives violate the naming contract** that's restated 7 times across the docs, and **37/38 have no usable agent transcripts** — `bin/orbit-session-archive` either never ran or its Codex/Grok/Claude capture silently failed. The four duplicate `dependency-audit` archives on mini are one loop re-archived 4 times because the script has no idempotency and mints UTC names.
- **The finalization gate passes broken packets**: free-prose outcomes, literal `pending` placeholders, even `HEAD == base` with an empty diff. It's also missing from the implementing-features workflow steps entirely.
- **Ceremony costs ~45% of orchestrator turns** (median), mostly polling workers and re-filling boilerplate — one session was 95% loop.md bookkeeping with zero implementation. Single-slice loops fill the full multi-slice template with "not applicable".
- **Skills have real staleness**: implementing-features references a root `vendor/bin/mago` that doesn't exist, command-designer mandates phantom classes agents write uncompilable code from, and 8 direct doc contradictions (e.g. analyzer before-merge vs after-merge).
- **The self-improvement pipes are disconnected**: the signal ledger has been frozen since 2026-06-25, loop-observer is referenced by nothing and contradicted by HARNESS.md, and no eval skill reads the session archives it was built to consume.

The scratchpad ranks 8 implementation slices; the top three (harden `orbit-session-archive`, harden `orbit-feature-finalization-check`, compact single-slice loop.md) replace roughly a dozen duplicated prose rules with tool enforcement — which is what the evidence says actually changes agent behavior. It also has a keep-list of the 8 load-bearing rules that shouldn't be touched.
